dz.headline: Algerian Security Services Launch Coordinated Campaign Against Neighborhood Gangs
dz.dek: Algeria's security services have initiated a more unified and forceful campaign against neighborhood gangs, moving beyond previous sporadic operations by police and gendarmerie.
paragraphs: Algeria's security services have launched a coordinated campaign against neighborhood gangs, following directives from President Abdelmadjid Tebboune. This new strategy aims to dismantle criminal networks in urban areas that have been threatening citizens' safety, spreading fear, and expanding into drug distribution.

The operations involve police and gendarmerie units conducting targeted raids on organized criminal group hideouts across the country. In Algiers, large-scale operations on Monday night, coinciding with the Prophet Muhammad’s birthday, targeted 13 administrative security districts.

These raids resulted in the arrest of numerous suspects and the seizure of bladed weapons, drugs, psychotropic substances, and criminal proceeds. Algiers security authorities reported dismantling six criminal networks comprising 42 people, confiscating 58 prohibited bladed weapons, cocaine, flares, marine distress signals, tear-gas canisters, and 218,000 Algerian dinars in cash.

dz.headline: Netanyahu, Katz Threaten Gaza Eviction Over Children's Toy Kites
dz.dek: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and War Minister Yisrael Katz have threatened to displace entire Gaza neighborhoods if children continue launching toy kites towards.
paragraphs: Netanyahu and Katz convened a "situation assessment session" on Sunday, August twenty-third, to discuss what they termed the "threat of launching balloons and paper planes from Gaza." This meeting included the Chief of Staff of the Israeli army, Eyal Zamir, the head of the National Security Council, and other senior military officials.

Katz reportedly directed the army to "act forcefully" against those launching the paper planes, evacuate neighborhoods and areas from which they are launched, and target "terrorist infrastructure" in those locations. He considers each launch a "full-fledged act of war," despite the kites carrying no explosives or incendiary materials.

The officials' reaction to children's toy kites, which they equate to military drones, has drawn surprise and ridicule. They have also threatened to expand assassinations against Hamas leaders if the kite launches do not cease, linking the children's activities to broader security concerns.

dz.headline: Windstorm capsizes pleasure boat, kills two and injures six in Béjaïa
dz.dek: A sudden weather deterioration with powerful waves and strong wind gusts caused a small pleasure craft to overturn off the west coast of Béjaïa.
paragraphs: Two vacationers died and six others were injured Monday evening when a pleasure boat capsized near the west coast of the wilaya of Béjaïa. The incident occurred around nineteen hours thirty as the weather conditions rapidly worsened, trapping the small vessel amidst strong waves and sustained wind gusts.

On the beach, witnesses and citizens quickly mobilized to assist the occupants of the overturned boat. However, the intensity of the waves and the strong currents hindered these initial rescue efforts by those present at the scene.

Civil Protection rescuers were promptly dispatched to the location, taking over to secure the area and provide care for the survivors. The event disrupted the calm of the seaside resort, leading to a spontaneous chain of mutual aid among those nearby.

dz.headline: Algerian Customs expands border control with new guard centers and inspectorates
dz.dek: Public authorities are tightening regulations at land, sea, and air borders to combat smuggling and enhance control over incoming goods.
paragraphs: Algeria has established new Customs guard centers at its land borders and increased the number of quality control and fraud suppression inspectorates to 53. The Director General of Customs, Major General Bakhouche, approved a decree on June 1, 2026, creating these centers to provide continuous field presence and operational support to Customs teams.

These new centers will operate day and night through a continuous patrol system, ensuring permanent guarding of adjacent border strips and coordinating with National Gendarmerie units to combat cross-border crimes. They are also tasked with securing seized goods until delivery to the competent Customs collector.

In coordination with the Ministry of Finance, the Ministry of Internal Trade and National Market Regulation has increased the deployment of quality control and fraud suppression services. This expansion involves replacing the previous list of inspectorate locations with a new one covering more outlets and sensitive sites across various provinces.

ao.headline: President Lourenço inaugurates Luanda convention center, urges private hotel investment
ao.dek: President João Lourenço opened a new convention center in Luanda, emphasizing its role in attracting international events and calling for private sector investment in the.
paragraphs: Angola's President João Lourenço inaugurated a new convention center in Luanda, built on land that was ocean three years ago. The facility, which includes an amphitheater with three thousand seats, is intended to host international events previously held in tents and hotels, according to the President.

The new Palace of Conventions features twelve halls, four of which are still unfinished, with one hall offering five hundred seats. President Lourenço stated that the center will elevate the country's image and support business tourism, highlighting Angola's increasing attractiveness for international events.

President Lourenço appealed to private investors to develop the tourism sector, specifically hotel infrastructure, noting that Luanda has few hotels. He stressed that any investment in hospitality would be insufficient given the current needs, emphasizing the government's focus on improving the business environment to attract capital.

ao.headline: Angola invites Brazilian firms to invest in local production
ao.dek: Angolan Secretary of State for Industry, Carlos Rodrigues, urged Brazilian businesses to establish production facilities in Angola, aiming to leverage the country as a gateway to.
paragraphs: Carlos Rodrigues, speaking at the Angola-Brazil Business Meeting 2026 in Luanda, encouraged Brazilian companies to consider Angola for investment, production, and as a platform for expanding into the African market. He stated the Angolan executive is ready to collaborate with Brazilian entrepreneurs to strengthen bilateral relations, building on decades of commercial ties.

Rodrigues emphasized Angola's desire for Brazilian companies to shift from solely trading to producing goods within the country. He highlighted the potential for Brazilian firms to process raw materials and form partnerships to develop local capacity, with the goal of reaching other African markets.

Angola is particularly interested in Brazil's assistance in developing agro-industrial complexes, combining agricultural production, research, technology, mechanization, logistics, and industrial processing. Rodrigues noted extensive business opportunities in areas like cereal, fruit, and coffee processing, edible oil production, animal protein transformation, and food industry equipment.

ao.headline: Angola enrolls unregistered children in schools after 50 years
ao.dek: The Ministry of Education has mandated public and private schools to enroll children without identification documents for the upcoming academic year, addressing a long-standing.
paragraphs: Angola's Ministry of Education has directed all public and private schools, from primary to secondary levels, to accept children for enrollment even if they lack identification documents. This measure, announced in a dispatch, responds to a large influx of school-aged children seeking enrollment for the next academic year without proper identification.

The Ministry's decision aims to prevent the non-presentation of documents from increasing the number of citizens outside the education system. Official data from 2024 indicated that about 60% of children in the country were not registered, highlighting the scale of the issue the new policy addresses.

Schools are now required to identify children without documents by the end of October 2026 and communicate this information to the Ministry of Justice and Human Rights' Identification, Records, and Notary Directorate. This directorate will then visit schools to register the children, while schools also educate families on the importance of civil registration and obtaining identity cards.

ao.headline: UNITA invite limits political activist's travel in Africa
ao.dek: An independent political activist accepted an invitation from UNITA to fill one of four vacancies on the CNE, which will restrict his political activities across Africa.
paragraphs: A political activist has accepted an invitation from UNITA to serve as an independent member on the CNE, filling one of four available positions. This new role will unfortunately limit his regular political travels and engagements across the continent, particularly in the Sahel region.

The activist has been critical of leaders who sell public assets to private entities, viewing the privatization of public companies as a "market crime" rather than market economy. He argues that countries with histories of slavery and colonialism, lacking developed education systems, should not privatize major public enterprises that serve as beacons for public policies in education, health, and entrepreneurship.

His work has focused on advocating for the transformation of African wealth, specifically rare earths, within each country. The new commitment means he will no longer be able to regularly visit countries like Senegal, Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger, Mozambique, and Malawi to the same extent as before.

ao.headline: Expo Cabinda Fails to Attract Investment, Creates Temporary Jobs
ao.dek: The Expo Cabinda event, intended to boost development, has instead been criticized for excluding local businesses, wasting public funds, and generating only temporary employment.
paragraphs: The Expo Cabinda, held at the Tafe Multipurpose Pavilion, has been described as a political illusion masking local governance failures and deep disparities. While large companies, many linked to political clientelism, showcased their portfolios, small producers in Cabinda were marginalized or excluded due to prohibitive participation costs, according to Folha 8. The event failed to foster Cabinda's real economy, instead legitimizing the monopoly of existing elites.

Millions of kwanzas were reportedly spent on temporary infrastructure, government advertising, and ceremonial banquets, representing a misdirection of public funds. This spending occurred in a territory where basic medicines are scarce, youth unemployment is high, and water and electricity supply remain critical issues. The Expo Cabinda, lasting only a few days, stands in contrast to the year-round misery in surrounding neighborhoods.

The event has not attracted serious external investment, with critics noting that investors are unlikely to be swayed by decorated pavilions when the region faces impassable roads and stifling bureaucracy. Memoranda of understanding signed at the expo reportedly serve only to generate state press headlines, with no lasting impact. The jobs created were mostly temporary, precarious, and informal, limited to the setup and dismantling of stands or event-focused catering, leaving Cabinda's youth to face unemployment after the expo concludes.

bj.headline: Abdoulaye Bio Tchané launches departmental CES activities in Borgou
bj.dek: The Economic and Social Council (CES) president began a national tour in Parakou to operationalize departmental CES branches and open their second ordinary session.
paragraphs: Abdoulaye Bio Tchané, president of the Economic and Social Council (CES), officially launched the activities of departmental CES branches on Tuesday, August twenty-fifth, 2026, in Parakou. This event, coupled with the opening of their second ordinary session, marks a new stage in the CES's transformation, following the start of its eighth mandate. The ceremony took place at the Parakou prefecture, attended by the Borgou prefect, departmental councilors, National Assembly deputies, and local mayors.

The Borgou prefect stated that the operationalization of the CES at the territorial level is a significant advancement that brings the institution closer to the population and their daily realities. President Bio Tchané emphasized four pillars for the CES's new dynamic: utility, citizen proximity, inter-institutional dialogue, and international outreach. He highlighted the adoption of internal regulations and the launch of the 2027-2031 strategic plan as decisive steps already taken.

The event in Parakou is the first stop on a tour that will take the presidential delegation to all twelve departmental capitals of Benin. Bio Tchané stated that the departmental councilors will serve as a link, explaining the CES to citizens and ensuring the population's voice is heard, thereby fostering local democracy.

bj.headline: Mathurin De Chacus concludes eight-year tenure as Benin football president
bj.dek: Mathurin De Chacus officially handed over leadership of Beninese football to his successor, Marcellin Bocovè, after two terms marked by significant development in the sport.
paragraphs: Mathurin De Chacus concluded his eight-year presidency of the Beninese Football Federation (FBF) on Tuesday, August 25, 2026, at the Elective General Assembly held at the Missérété Football Excellence Center. He transferred authority to Marcellin Bocovè, who acknowledged De Chacus's contributions to the sport.

During his tenure, De Chacus oversaw the construction of stadiums, the establishment of excellence centers, and the training of coaches. Marcellin Bocovè noted that statutory competitions were organized, youth opportunities expanded, women's football gained prominence, and clubs received support.

Bocovè also highlighted that De Chacus's leadership ensured the federation operated without crises, a point of pride for the outgoing president, who expressed happiness in setting an example for a smooth transition of power in Beninese football.

bj.headline: Madagascar civil society fears Russian election interference
bj.dek: Civil society groups in Madagascar express concern over Russia's offer of technical support for the 2027 presidential election, citing past actions in the Central African Republic.
paragraphs: Concerns are rising among some civil society members in Madagascar regarding Russia's proposal to provide technical assistance for the 2027 Malagasy presidential election. Critics view this offer as part of an influence strategy previously observed in the Central African Republic, where increased Russian presence reshaped political and security dynamics.

In the Central African Republic, Moscow's "technical support" for the National Election Agency reportedly led to systematic ballot stuffing, direct threats against opponents of Faustin Archange Touadera, and targeted intimidation of the ruling party's adversaries. Russian forces, identified as Wagner, secured polling stations in strategic areas, controlled voter flows, and ensured official results aligned with Kremlin interests, leading to a presidential re-election deemed incredible by most independent observers.

The current rapprochement between Madagascar's transitional authorities and the Kremlin fuels debate on the risks of foreign interference in a process intended to restore constitutional order. Critics suggest the Russian offer is a maneuver to meddle in Madagascar's internal affairs and manipulate election results in favor of a chosen candidate, rather than supporting democratic transition.

bj.dek: An investigation has commenced in Forécariah, Guinea, following the discovery of six unidentified male bodies in a pit in Sabakhouré on August twenty-fourth, 2026.
paragraphs: Six unidentified male bodies were found in a pit in Sabakhouré, within the sub-prefecture of Allassoyah, prompting local authorities and a prosecutor to visit the scene. The discovery led to an immediate alert from residents in the Forécariah area.

The initial local reports have not established the identities of the victims or the exact circumstances of their deaths. This lack of information prevents attributing a motive or identifying perpetrators in connection with the discovery.

The bodies have been transferred to the Forécariah prefectural hospital. This transfer is a necessary step for the judicial inquiry and the identification process to proceed, according to local reports from Benin Web TV.

bj.headline: Owner of Avakpa fuel cargo identified after August 6 fire
bj.dek: The owner of the adulterated fuel cargo involved in the August 6 fire in Avakpa, Porto-Novo, has been identified and questioned, according to local media reports.
paragraphs: Following the August 6 to 7, 2026, fire in Avakpa, Porto-Novo, caused by Kpayo fuel, the owner of the cargo has been identified and interviewed. The incident, which resulted in significant material damage, involved a truck carrying barrels of adulterated fuel that reportedly struck an electrical pole before igniting.

Local media reports indicate that the owner's identification was possible due to customs records. Any such cargo crossing Beninese borders must be registered with customs services, making it difficult to conceal ownership or involvement in the incident. This traceability is expected to help determine responsibility.

Despite public speculation about potential interference in the investigation to downplay the incident or secure leniency for the cargo owners, authorities state that such attempts would be impossible. No deaths were reported in the fire, which involved an explosion of the fuel barrels.

bw.headline: Chief Justice warns Law Society over Foot-and-Mouth Disease legal intervention
bw.dek: Chief Justice Gaolapelwe Ketlogetswe cautioned the Law Society of Botswana against interfering in a high-profile legal dispute related to the FMD crisis.
paragraphs: Chief Justice Gaolapelwe Ketlogetswe has warned the Law Society of Botswana (LSB) against intervening in a significant legal dispute stemming from the Foot-and-Mouth Disease (FMD) crisis. This warning followed Ketlogetswe's dismissal of an urgent application by the LSB, which sought to reverse his decision to allow South African Senior Counsel Reginald Willis to practice in Botswana on an ad hoc basis.

Willis had been granted permission to represent JS Beef (Pty) Ltd and Primefast (Pty) Ltd in urgent litigation. This litigation concerns the government's management and the economic consequences of the FMD outbreak, indicating ongoing legal challenges related to the disease's impact.

The Chief Justice's stance highlights a judicial pushback against the LSB's involvement in a case that directly affects businesses dealing with the economic fallout of the FMD crisis, signaling potential implications for legal representation in such high-stakes disputes.

bw.headline: Botswana fertility rate falls below replacement level
bw.dek: Botswana's total fertility rate has dropped to 1.96 children per woman, falling below the 2.1 replacement level benchmark, according to the 2024 Vital Statistics Report.
paragraphs: Botswana is experiencing a demographic shift as its total fertility rate has fallen below the population replacement level. The 2024 Vital Statistics Report from Statistics Botswana indicates the rate is now 1.96 children per woman, which is below the 2.1 benchmark needed to maintain a stable population.

This change suggests a future challenge for the country, which has historically focused on creating jobs for a growing youth population. The gradual decline in births, occurring one family at a time, points to a potentially significant long-term demographic transformation.

The shift implies that Botswana may soon face a different problem: a shortage of young people. This contrasts with decades of effort to address youth unemployment, signaling a reversal in demographic trends that could impact various sectors of the economy and society.

bw.headline: Government seeks P3.1 billion in August debt auction
bw.dek: The Ministry of Finance aims to raise P3.1 billion from the domestic market on August twenty-eighth to fund the budget deficit, continuing its reliance on monthly debt auctions.
paragraphs: The government plans to secure P3.1 billion from the domestic market on August twenty-eighth through a debt auction. This move continues the government's strategy of using monthly debt auctions to finance its budget deficit, as reported by the Sunday Standard.

The Bank of Botswana will conduct the auction on behalf of the Ministry of Finance. The offering is part of the existing P55 billion domestic note programme and includes P1.5 billion in three-month Treasury bills due on December two, 2026, and P1 billion in six-month bills maturing on March three, 2027.

Additionally, the auction will offer P600 million in reopened longer-term government bonds. This financing effort highlights the government's ongoing need for capital from the domestic market to meet its financial obligations.

bw.headline: Botswana citizenship-by-investment program stalls, leaving applicants in limbo
bw.dek: Botswana's Impact Citizenship Program, intended to offer citizenship for financial contributions, has not launched as scheduled, leaving prospective investors unable to apply.
paragraphs: Botswana's planned citizenship-by-investment program, marketed as the Impact Citizenship Program, has failed to open on schedule, according to DirectCitizenship.com. The program, which was promoted as a fast-track entry to citizenship in exchange for a financial contribution, is not yet operational and is not accepting applications.

The delay means that would-be investors are currently in limbo. The government is still working to finalize the legal, institutional, and administrative machinery required to launch the scheme, which has raised questions about its readiness for international investors.
What was initially presented as a quick path to Botswana citizenship has instead become a prolonged delay, impacting those who had anticipated applying to the program.

bf.headline: Burkina Faso Muslims Celebrate Prophet Mohammad's Birth with Prayers for Peace
bf.dek: Muslim faithful across Burkina Faso, including in the Liptako region, observed Maouloud 2026 with religious teachings and invocations for national peace and social cohesion.
paragraphs: Muslim communities in Burkina Faso commemorated Maouloud 2026, the night of the Prophet Mohammad's birth, on August twenty-fifth and twenty-sixth. The observance, mirroring practices in other countries, featured readings from the Holy Quran, prayers, public conferences, and blessings. Religious leaders emphasized the Prophet's life as an example of love, peace, and tolerance for humanity.

In Dori, the capital of the Liptako region, numerous faithful gathered at the city's grand mosque for a vigil of religious instruction focused on the Prophet Muhammad's life and work. Imam Yaya Mamoudou Cissé led the ritual, which included individual and collective invocations for the return of peace, unity, and social cohesion in Burkina Faso.

The celebration served as an occasion for Muslims to reinforce their faith and cultivate values of tolerance, understanding, and solidarity within the community. Participants prayed for the country's stability, expressing hopes for its people to live in tranquility and fraternity, according to the Agence d'Information du Burkina.

bf.headline: Bobo-Dioulasso market fire prompts toxic chemical warning
bf.dek: An early morning fire at the Grand Marché in Bobo-Dioulasso, specifically in a store selling pesticides and herbicides, has led to a warning about toxic contamination.
paragraphs: An early morning fire on Tuesday, August twenty-fifth, 2026, at the Grand Marché in Bobo-Dioulasso, sector one, destroyed a significant quantity of pesticides and other chemicals. The blaze, which started around two o'clock in the morning, affected a commercial zone in the Diarradougou neighborhood.

The President of the Special Communal Delegation (PDS), Laurent Kontogom, issued a warning to residents, merchants, and users of the area to exercise extreme caution due to risks of intoxication and contamination. Competent environmental and agricultural services have confirmed the presence of highly toxic and dangerous substances released during the fire and extinction process.

Authorities have implemented temporary closures of surrounding businesses and isolated the affected zone with a security perimeter. An emergency team at the Bobo-Dioulasso City Hall is coordinating interventions, assessing risks, and proposing measures for site remediation. The public is advised to strictly follow safety instructions and avoid contact with any spilled or potentially contaminated materials.

bf.headline: Police seize 20 million FCFA in contraband goods in Nahouri
bf.dek: Law enforcement in Pô dismantled three smuggling groups, confiscating cigarettes, fertilizer, fuel, and adulterated beverages valued at nearly 20 million FCFA.
paragraphs: Burkinabe police forces in Pô, operating under WIBGA III, broke up three alleged smuggling rings trafficking goods between Burkina Faso and a neighboring country. The operation resulted in the seizure of 1,350 cartons of cigarettes, 600 bags of fertilizer, fuel, and adulterated beverages, with an estimated total value of nearly 20 million FCFA.

The police intercepted a tricycle carrying four 25-liter cans of gasoline, three cartons of liquor, and twelve bottles of adulterated beverages. They also stopped a vehicle with 1,350 cartons of GOLD Searl cigarettes and three other vehicles, each transporting ten tons of chemical fertilizer, totaling 600 fifty-kilogram bags.

Investigations revealed that these groups sourced large quantities of contraband from a neighboring country and resold them in various Burkinabe cities, including Dakola, Pô, Kombissiri, and Ouagadougou. The National Police thanked citizens for their cooperation, which contributed to the success of the operation.

bf.headline: Traoré urges AES deputies to prioritize public interest
bf.dek: Captain Ibrahim Traoré, current President of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES), called on confederate deputies to prioritize the general interest of the AES over partisan and.
paragraphs: The first session of the Parliament of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) opened yesterday, August twenty-fourth, 2026, with a call from Captain Ibrahim Traoré for deputies to defend the superior interest of the people. Speaking through Ousmane Bougma, president of the People's Legislative Assembly, Traoré urged the 45 deputies, 15 from each member country, to focus on the collective good.

The session, running from August twenty-fourth to twenty-ninth, 2026, aims to establish a framework for parliamentary cooperation among Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger. These three nations formed the AES in August 2024, seven months after leaving ECOWAS in January 2024, to strengthen their collective efforts against terrorism, defend sovereignty, and promote endogenous development.

Traoré emphasized that the path chosen by the AES demands unity of action, clear vision, bold decisions, and fraternity. He exhorted deputies to thoroughly examine the issues on the agenda, underscoring the importance of their role in building the confederation's parliamentary institutions.

bf.headline: ARSN inspects Clinique les Oliviers radiology unit for compliance
bf.dek: The National Authority for Radioprotection and Nuclear Safety (ARSN) conducted a pre-authorization inspection of the radiology facilities at Clinique les Oliviers in Ouagadougou.
paragraphs: An ARSN team, led by National Director Belko Massi Barry, inspected the radiology department at Clinique les Oliviers on Tuesday, August twenty-fifth, 2026. This pre-authorization mission aims to verify the conformity of the installations, the radiology equipment, and protective devices before their operational authorization, following a request from the clinic to operate its standard radiology machine.

Inspectors examined the radiology room's conformity, collective protection barriers, individual protective equipment, and personnel dosimetric surveillance devices. They also checked registers for work procedures, maintenance, and quality control of equipment. Quality control tests were performed to verify technical characteristics and ensure compliance with radioprotection requirements, according to Dr. Yaméogo Zakaria, Head of the Inspections, Control, and Radiological Surveillance Division at ARSN.

The clinic's deputy general director, Tanga Ouédraogo, welcomed the inspection, stating it will enhance protection for patients and workers and contribute to public health. ARSN will send a letter to the clinic detailing any deficiencies and corrective measures needed, and the clinic has expressed readiness to implement recommendations and strengthen staff skills.

bi.headline: Fire ravages Kinindo market in Bujumbura, destroying goods
bi.dek: A fire broke out in the Kinindo market in southern Bujumbura on Tuesday, destroying merchandise and causing significant losses for several traders, just days after a similar.
paragraphs: A fire erupted around 10 AM in the mattress section of Kinindo market, a key commercial hub in Burundi's economic capital. Firefighters, the Red Cross, and disaster management services responded quickly, bringing the blaze under control within an hour, but a portion of the goods was destroyed.

The incident follows a major fire last Friday that devastated two commercial galleries in downtown Bujumbura. Finance Minister Alain Ndikumana visited the scene, stating the fire's cause is unknown and an investigation has begun. He assured that the government would monitor the situation and consider support measures for affected traders.

Antoine Muzaneza, president of the Association of Traders of Burundi (ACOBU), urged authorities to enhance market security, proposing security committees, controlled opening hours, and surveillance cameras. Police increased security at Kinindo market to prevent looting amid the confusion caused by the fire.

bi.headline: Police actions lead to two deaths in Bugendana, Gitega province
bi.dek: Two individuals died in Bugendana commune, Gitega province, following a police intervention and a violent assault, prompting local demands for independent investigations.
paragraphs: Désiré Nshimirimana, 25, died from a gunshot wound during a police intervention on Gaterama hill on Tuesday, August 25. Heavily armed police officers had gone to Joseph Bandora's home to make arrests related to a land dispute, according to a witness. The intervention escalated when residents opposed the police, leading to a police officer allegedly firing a shot that hit Nshimirimana in the chest, killing him instantly.

Following the incident, residents blocked the Bugendana-Kibimba road for nearly two hours, interrupting traffic. Six individuals—Duido Nahimana, Venant Ndayisenga, Olivier Nkurunziza, Remy Bigirimana, Édouard Bigirimana, and Rénovat Nimbona—were arrested and taken to police cells for investigation. Romuald Habonimana, chief of Gaterama hill, confirmed the events and the subsequent tension.

Separately, Isaac Habonimana, 39, died two days earlier on Sunday, August 23, on Gitongo hill after being severely beaten. Dieudonné Bizimana, chief of Gitongo hill, stated that Habonimana was accused of disturbing security in a bistro. Raphaël Nduwimana, the chief of the Gitongo police post, was identified as the alleged assailant and has since been arrested and taken to police cells in Bugendana.

bi.headline: Burundi President Criticizes Mining, Commerce Ministries' Performance
bi.dek: President Ndayishimiye expressed deep disappointment with the commerce and mining sectors, stating they appear "non-existent" and contribute nothing to the country's wealth.
paragraphs: President Ndayishimiye, speaking on August fourteen, two thousand twenty-six, at Ntare House in Bujumbura, criticized high-ranking officials from the Ministry of Mineral Resources, Energy, Industry, Commerce, and Tourism. He stated that the commerce and mining sectors seem "non-existent" and contribute nothing to Burundi's wealth, despite their potential.

The President also targeted managers at Regideso, the public utility, for allegedly sharing dividends after budget exercises without contributing capital. He accused Regideso of corruption, citing instances where customers seeking electricity or meters were required to pay bribes. Ndayishimiye announced that the General Inspectorate would investigate Regideso's accounts.

Furthermore, the President lamented that the head of Sotrevo Mining Limited failed to execute an order worth one hundred forty-seven thousand dollars, despite sufficient liquidity. Sotrevo, which holds an industrial mining permit for Cassiterite, Colombo-Tantalite, and associated minerals in Murehe, was expected to be a significant revenue source for the country, but its management did not meet expectations.

bi.headline: M23 and Twirwaneho Fighters Seize FARDC Positions in Bijombo
bi.dek: Clashes in Bijombo, South Kivu, led to the reported capture of several strategic locations previously held by Congolese forces and Wazalendo militias.
paragraphs: Fighters identified by local sources as affiliated with Twirwaneho and M23 reportedly took control of positions in Rubarati, Ruhuha, and Malimba on Sunday. These areas were previously occupied by elements of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) and Wazalendo militiamen in the Bijombo groupement, Uvira territory. The information, which could not be independently verified, suggests a displacement of combatants from various camps following the confrontations.

Sources from the Masango area claim some fighters involved in the offensive arrived from Muramvya, Kashongo, Kageregere, and Mukumba. FARDC elements reportedly retreated towards the Munanira mountains, while Wazalendo militiamen moved towards Masango. Local sources also reported the abandonment of several weapons during the retreat. Representatives of civil society in Uvira territory further allege that Burundian Red Tabara fighters participated alongside Twirwaneho/M23 elements, though this claim remains unconfirmed.

Local analysts believe the potential capture of Malimba, Ruhuha, and Rubarati holds strategic importance for controlling the Uvira highlands and routes connecting several South Kivu localities. These positions could facilitate movements towards Bukavu, Kaziba, Rurambo, and Minembwe, and offer access to the Ruzizi plain and heights overlooking Uvira city. These assessments are analytical and do not confirm military progression into these areas.

bi.headline: Jadot Nkurunziza mobilizes youth for environmental cleanup in Bujumbura
bi.dek: Jadot Nkurunziza, known as "Giti," organizes young people in Ntahangwa commune to remove water hyacinth from Lake Tanganyika and promote urban cleanliness.
paragraphs: Jadot Nkurunziza, a native of Nyakabiga, is actively engaging residents in environmental efforts across Bujumbura. He is recognized for his work in the Ntahangwa commune, where he sensitizes youth on sanitation and flower planting along Mwezi Gisabo Boulevard, according to local residents.

His efforts extend to Lake Tanganyika, where he mobilizes young people to remove water hyacinth, which can threaten local activities and the ecosystem. Residents near the lake describe him as a "hero" for organizing these clean-up initiatives, which they say are uncommon in their community.

Nkurunziza's commitment to the environment stems from his childhood, where his grandfather taught him the importance of trees for fruits, respiration, energy, and construction materials. After studying environmental protection in Uganda, he returned to Burundi to apply his knowledge locally, including managing a nursery by the Ntahangwa River with various plants and trees.

cm.headline: Léonide Mfoum resigns from UNDP after 12 years of activism
cm.dek: Léonide Mfoum, a national communication cell member, cited a lack of debate and party direction as reasons for his departure from the Union Nationale pour la Démocratie et le.
paragraphs: Léonide Mfoum has resigned from the Union Nationale pour la Démocratie et le Progrès (UNDP) after 12 years, effective August twenty-fifth, 2026. He stated his refusal to be led by “incompetents” and described the party as having “no horizon, no perspective.” Mfoum also criticized the party's inability to engage in debate, which he believes hinders progress and future planning.

Mfoum attributed his resignation to the party's failure in the 2025 presidential election, where candidate Bello Bouba Maigari placed fourth with 2.45% of the votes. He blamed party leaders for refusing self-reflection and criticism, which he called the “cancer” of the party. Mfoum specifically pointed to the campaign director, suggesting a lack of understanding of the role.

Despite the electoral setback, Mfoum claims no lessons were learned within the UNDP, and the same leadership continued. He denounced party leaders as having “adulterated depth” and being willing to sideline bright minds who could pose a challenge. His departure comes ahead of the 2027 municipal and legislative elections, though he did not indicate his next political move.

cm.headline: Canyon Resources postpones bauxite production amid financial dispute
cm.dek: Canyon Resources has indefinitely delayed its Minim-Martap bauxite project in Cameroon, citing a frozen credit line and a hostile takeover bid.
paragraphs: Canyon Resources announced on Monday, August twenty-fourth, 2026, that it is postponing the start of bauxite production at its Minim-Martap project, which was initially scheduled for the fourth quarter of 2026. The company's CEO, Peter Secker, will depart by the end of August, indicating internal governance issues.

The delay stems from AFG Bank Cameroon freezing an 82 billion FCFA ($140 million) credit line essential for operations. This financial blockage coincides with a hostile takeover attempt by A2MP Investments, led by Gagan Gupta, which already holds 55.56% of Canyon Resources' capital. A2MP Investments has launched a bid to acquire full control at a discounted price of 0.05 Australian dollars per share, arguing that rising logistical costs make the project unprofitable.

Despite these financial and corporate challenges, the physical infrastructure for the project is largely complete. The mining road is finished, and 60 wagons ordered from China are expected to arrive in Douala in October. The Minim-Martap deposit, containing 1.1 billion tons of bauxite, is ready for extraction, leaving the Cameroonian state, which anticipated bauxite exports to offset declining oil revenues, in a prolonged wait for the project's commencement.

cm.headline: Minesup restricts professional license admissions to private higher education institutions
cm.dek: Minister of Higher Education Jacques Fame Ndongo has reinforced the requirement for a two-year post-Baccalaureate qualification for professional license programs, targeting.
paragraphs: The Ministry of Higher Education (Minesup) has tightened admission rules for professional licenses, prohibiting private higher education institutions (IPES) from admitting students without a Bac+2 level qualification. This directive, issued on August twenty-first, two thousand twenty-six, aims to uphold the LMD system standard, which mandates six semesters of study for a license.

Minister Jacques Fame Ndongo's communication specifies that professional licenses are accessible only to candidates holding a valid two-year post-secondary diploma, such as a DEUG, BTS, HND, or DUT. The minister noted that some IPES have been admitting Baccalaureate holders and granting them a license after just one year of study, which contradicts the established regulations.

This measure comes weeks before the two thousand twenty-six/two thousand twenty-seven academic year and warns IPES promoters to strictly adhere to the rule to avoid sanctions. The ministry emphasizes that this enforcement is crucial for maintaining the quality of education, preserving student standards, and ensuring their competitiveness in the job market, addressing concerns about declining academic levels.

cm.headline: SCDP inaugurates three new infrastructures to boost energy supply
cm.dek: The Société Camerounaise des Dépôts Pétroliers (SCDP) launched a gas sphere, a pipeline, and a new headquarters in Douala to enhance national energy security.
paragraphs: The Société Camerounaise des Dépôts Pétroliers (SCDP) inaugurated three major infrastructures on Friday, August twenty-first, 2026, in Douala. These include a new domestic gas sphere in Bonabéri, a pipeline connecting the Port of Douala to the Bessengué depot, and a new company headquarters. The Minister of Water and Energy, Gaston Eloundou Essomba, presided over the ceremony alongside SCDP Director General Véronique Manzoua épouse Moampea Mbio.

The new gas sphere in Bonabéri increases Cameroon's national gas storage capacity by forty percent, aiming to prevent shortages of cooking gas for households. The pipeline from the Port of Douala to Bessengué is designed to accelerate the unloading of oil tankers, streamline the logistics chain, and reduce fuel supply pressures across the country.

Minister Eloundou Essomba stated that these investments mark a shift from reactive management to an approach based on anticipation, resilience, and energy sovereignty. The new headquarters symbolizes the public company's transformation, reinforcing efforts to secure daily life for Cameroonians by improving fuel and gas availability.

paragraphs: The maternity ward at Bangui Community Hospital is experiencing changes in its operations and the care provided to women following the withdrawal of Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF). Hospital director Abel Assaye addressed these impacts in an interview with Astrid de Bonheur Kolengué.

Assaye detailed how MSF's departure has altered the hospital's capacity to manage maternity services. The organization had previously played a role in supporting the functioning of the ward and the provision of care for women seeking medical attention.

The discussion focused specifically on the practical consequences for the hospital's ability to maintain its previous level of service in the maternity department. The interview aimed to clarify the current situation for patients and staff at the facility.

cf.headline: Moloua's Security Plan Fails to Curb Rising Violence
cf.dek: Three months after Prime Minister Félix Moloua's security assurances, armed attacks, kidnappings, and killings continue to plague several regions of the Central African Republic.
paragraphs: Security in the Central African Republic has deteriorated, despite Prime Minister Félix Moloua's earlier commitment to deputies to restore peace using national forces, MINUSCA, and Russian and Rwandan allies. Recent events, including the June 29 killing of Vicar Crépin Monga in Haut-Mbomou by A Zandés Ani Kpi Gbé militiamen, highlight the ongoing instability.

The situation is particularly dire in the northeast, where a June 30 attack by the ASP rebel coalition on Amdafock resulted in at least 28 deaths and displaced nearly 18,000 civilians, according to the UN. Near Birao, unidentified armed men attacked Matala village, causing deaths and injuries, as reported by Moussa Radjab, deputy mayor of Birao.

Pockets of insecurity also persist in Ombella-Mpoko and Ouham-Fafa, where elements assimilated to the 3R terrorize residents. Near Bangui, a Swiss geologist and his aide were assassinated on July 30 at the Gbango-Carrière mining site. The government is responding by strengthening the national army, with 600 new recruits presented on August 10.

cf.headline: Former Deputy Mara States CAR Lacks National Culture
cf.dek: Jean-Pierre Mara, former deputy of Mala, asserted that the Central African Republic has never developed a common cultural project since its modern state formation.
paragraphs: Former deputy Jean-Pierre Mara claimed on November seven, two thousand twenty-five, that the Central African Republic has not built its own national culture. He stated that the country's founding president, Barthélemy Boganda, initially envisioned a federal entity for French Equatorial Africa, but this project failed due to a lack of regional consensus. Boganda then named a limited territory the Central African Republic without a strong cultural foundation.

Mara argued that this fragile beginning led to a state based on strictly political logic, adopting imported institutions without deep connections to local practices. He noted that successive constitutions mirrored Western models, ignoring the languages, rites, and specific needs of the Central African populations.

According to Mara, a national culture requires a mastered language, shared norms, and artistic forms representing a collective. He concluded that the Central African Republic lacks these conditions, citing linguistic disunity, limited written Sango, and ethnic diversity as barriers to building a common cultural base, which hinders the state's ability to mobilize citizens and implement lasting public policies.

ci.headline: Deputy Explains National Assembly Functions to Guitry Residents
ci.dek: Kouassi Koffi Kra Paulin, a deputy from Sorobango and Tagadi, detailed the National Assembly's roles and operations to the people of Guitry during a parliamentary outreach session.
paragraphs: Deputy Kouassi Koffi Kra Paulin explained the National Assembly's four main missions: representing citizens, voting on laws, overseeing government actions, and evaluating public policies. This session, held at the Lorka Dadié cultural center in Guitry on Saturday, August twenty-second, two thousand twenty-six, was part of a parliamentary restitution initiative championed by the institution's president, Patrick Achi.

The deputy also outlined the process for adopting laws, from committee review to parliamentary approval and promulgation, including the Senate's role when required. He emphasized the deputies' function in examining and amending government-initiated bills. The event was organized by Deputy Yao Patricia Sylvie, the first vice-president of the National Assembly and deputy for Guitry and Dairo-Didizo.

Looking ahead, Kra Paulin discussed planned investments in the Lôh-Djiboua region, focusing on renewable energy, biomass, road infrastructure, and agriculture. He announced the establishment of an agropole in Lôh-Djiboua to promote agricultural mechanization, local product processing, and food sovereignty. He also urged residents to secure land rights to prevent conflicts and promoted the social and solidarity economy for income-generating activities.

ci.headline: Abobo Church Council President Pledges Christian Unity
ci.dek: Bishop Lougah Mabé, the new president of the Abobo High Church Council, committed to strengthening Christian unity and cohesion during his investiture ceremony on Saturday.
paragraphs: Bishop Lougah Mabé assumed leadership of the Abobo High Church Council, promising to foster unity among Christians in the commune. His investiture took place at ADO Square, where he also thanked municipal authorities, including Abobo Mayor Kandia Camara.

Mayor Camara urged the Christian community to utilize state-provided opportunities for employment, entrepreneurship, and project financing. She encouraged religious leaders to share this information with their congregants to promote participation in empowerment and integration programs.

The new president stated that this drive for unity would enable member churches of the High Council to contribute more effectively to Abobo's social and community development. The ceremony was attended by administrative and customary authorities, alongside numerous faithful from various member churches.

ci.headline: PDCI Vice-President Urges Restraint Amidst Internal Party Tensions
ci.dek: Michel Gueu, a vice-president of the PDCI-RDA, has called for dialogue and respect for party institutions as internal disputes escalate.
paragraphs: The Parti démocratique de Côte d'Ivoire (PDCI-RDA) is experiencing internal turmoil, prompting Michel Gueu, a vice-president, to urge party members to exercise restraint. Gueu specifically called for dialogue and respect for the party's established bodies, according to Linfodrome on August 24, 2026.

This appeal comes as the party faces significant internal challenges, including a court decision expected on October 22 regarding the potential removal of the PDCI president. Jeune Afrique reported on August 25, 2026, that numerous cyberactivists are actively defending Tidjane Thiam, a presidential candidate for the PDCI in 2025, across social media platforms like TikTok, Facebook, and X.

Gueu also advised party executives to avoid escalating rhetoric and to prioritize mediation as a means to resolve the ongoing internal disagreements. The party's reliance on cyberactivists to defend its candidate highlights a shift in political engagement strategies within the PDCI.

ci.headline: Diogo Bamba assumes leadership of Dozo traditional hunters in Ivory Coast
ci.dek: Diogo Bamba was inaugurated as the national chief of the Dozo traditional hunters in Tokala, succeeding Fadjouma Bamba and committing to unity and collaboration with defense.
paragraphs: Diogo Bamba was installed as the national chief of the Dozo traditional hunters of Ivory Coast on Thursday, August 20, 2026, in Tokala, within the sub-prefecture of Mahadianan-Sokourani. The ceremony, sponsored by the chief of the Vandougou canton and observed by military authorities, saw Bamba pledge to unify the hunters and harmonize their actions with the defense and security forces (FDS). He also proposed a national identification card for members to improve organization and state recognition.

Bamba emphasized that the Dozos' role in security is a civilian support to the FDS, not a replacement for their sovereign missions, stating that a Dozo hunter is not an FDS agent but collaborates to enhance security across Ivory Coast. He urged members to act exemplarily and respect national institutions, viewing security as a collective responsibility.

Noumoutié Koné, president and national spokesperson for the National Council of the Dozo Binkadi Vandougou Traditional Hunters Brotherhood of Ivory Coast (CNCCTBV-CI), criticized the proliferation of traditional hunter associations, which he believes causes disorder. Koné called on Dozos to avoid illegal activities like selling weapons or drugs and to promote social cohesion, inviting all associations to join the national council.

eg.headline: Egypt showcases water scarcity solutions at UN desertification conference
eg.dek: Egypt's Water Resources and Irrigation Minister Hani Sewilam presented the country's strategies for water-use efficiency and climate adaptation at the UNCCD COP17 in Mongolia.
paragraphs: Egypt is sharing its experience in addressing water scarcity and climate adaptation at the 17th Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD COP17) in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia. Minister Hani Sewilam participated in the high-level segment, emphasizing the interconnectedness of water, land, climate, and food security, which requires integrated policies.

Sewilam highlighted Egypt's efforts to improve water-use efficiency, expand the reuse of agricultural drainage water, and implement climate adaptation projects. The country is also increasing its use of technology and innovation to manage its limited water resources. He stressed the need to move beyond crisis response and strengthen preparedness against climate-related pressures.

On the sidelines of the conference, Sewilam discussed cooperation in water resources management with Mongolian Minister of Food, Agriculture and Light Industry Tsagaankhuugiin Iderbat. The discussion included Egypt’s vision for implementing the second generation of its water management system (2.0), which integrates engineering and technological solutions to maximize the return on each unit of water, especially in agriculture.

eg.headline: FRA suspends finance firm, revokes CEO license over data breach
eg.dek: Egypt's Financial Regulatory Authority has initiated criminal proceedings and imposed a one-month ban on new contracts for a consumer finance company that exploited parents’ data.
paragraphs: The Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) has suspended a consumer finance company from issuing new contracts for one month and revoked its chief executive's license. This action follows an intensive four-day investigation into reports that the company used parents’ data to issue unauthorized loans for an international school, violating customer data, corporate governance, credit control, and anti-money laundering regulations.

The FRA's technical teams conducted on-site inspections and inquiries, leading to the cancellation of financial and credit liabilities wrongfully attached to affected parents. The regulator also banned the company from dealing in finance products related to school fees and club memberships, prohibiting new financing in these areas until a comprehensive regulatory review is complete.

In addition to these administrative measures, the FRA has formally notified the Public Prosecution, which is conducting ongoing criminal investigations. The authority also ordered the company’s general assembly to convene to address the violations and enforce stricter internal controls, emphasizing its commitment to protecting consumers from illegal practices.

eg.headline: Egypt coordinates economic policies, approves digital identity system
eg.dek: Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly and CBE Governor Hassan Abdalla met to align economic, fiscal, monetary, and sectoral policies for the National Economic Transformation Program.
paragraphs: Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly affirmed full coordination between the government and the Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) during a meeting with CBE Governor Hassan Abdalla on Monday, August 24, 2026. The coordination is part of preparations for the National Economic Transformation Program, aiming to integrate economic, fiscal, monetary, and sectoral policies to achieve a tangible impact on the national economy, as directed by President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi.

The meeting, held at the government headquarters in New Alamein City, reviewed the performance of the Egyptian economy, focusing on efforts to reduce inflation rates, increase dollar inflows, and strengthen foreign currency reserves. Officials confirmed that Egypt maintains safe levels of foreign currency reserves to secure strategic needs for essential commodities, with ongoing efforts to bolster strategic stocks through government and CBE coordination.

Separately, Governor Abdalla announced that the CBE Board of Directors approved regulations for the Digital Financial Identity System. This system allows banks to identify customers and verify identities electronically, supporting digital transformation and financial inclusion. The regulations establish a framework covering governance, roles, technical requirements, data protection, and cybersecurity to ensure secure and efficient service delivery.

paragraphs: Egypt has climbed to fifth place in the overall medal standings at the Mediterranean Games in Taranto, surpassing Spain, France, Croatia, and Serbia. The country's delegation, comprising 196 athletes, has earned a total of 13 medals, including four gold, four silver, and five bronze.

The medals were achieved across three sports: swimming, fencing, and wrestling. Notable performances include gold medals from Abdelrahman Sameh in 50m butterfly, Mohamed al-Sayed in épée, Mohamed Hamza in foil, and Mohamed Hassan in 67kg wrestling.

This performance highlights a strategy of focusing on a strong delegation rather than a large one, according to Minister of Youth and Sports Gohar Nabil and Egyptian Olympic Committee President Yasser Idris. Egypt also maintains its lead in the Arab medal standings, five medals ahead of Tunisia.

eg.headline: Private Sector Secures 60% of Investments as Economic Risk Falls
eg.dek: Egypt's Finance Minister Ahmed Kouchouk announced that the private sector now accounts for nearly 60% of total investments, driven by improving economic indicators.
paragraphs: The private sector in Egypt now holds nearly 60% of all investments, according to Finance Minister Ahmed Kouchouk. This increase comes as international risk assessments have reached their lowest levels since 2014, reflecting improved economic indicators. Kouchouk briefed Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly on the ministry's portfolio, highlighting the positive impact of state-led economic reforms on investor confidence.

The minister noted strong activity in the industrial, telecommunications, information technology, and tourism sectors, positioning the private sector as a key partner in economic development. The government plans to continue offering tax and customs incentives to support corporate expansion, stimulate production, and boost employment rates.

To enhance investment flows and attract foreign capital, the ministry is expanding premium tax centers and accelerating digital integration. This includes the launch of a new “Real Estate Dispositions” application, allowing citizens to complete property transactions online, from registration and document uploads to tax payments and final clearance, reducing the need for physical office visits.

gq.headline: Judiciary accused of inflating labor indemnities in Equatorial Guinea
gq.dek: A report alleges a judicial mechanism inflates labor indemnities, potentially benefiting courts and increasing costs for companies like Marathon Oil.
paragraphs: A judicial mechanism is allegedly inflating labor indemnities in Equatorial Guinea, according to a publication. The claim centers on a case involving Hermenegildo Esono Anguezomo, a former Government Relations Manager for Marathon, whose dismissal led to a court order for the company to pay 1,520,154,184 CFA francs in compensation, plus 45,604,625 CFA francs in legal costs.

Marathon appealed the ruling to the Supreme Court of Justice, citing an error of law. To appeal, the company had to deposit 1,878,910,572 CFA francs, which included the original judgment plus an additional 20%. The core of the complaint is that the Malabo Labor Court No. 2 calculated salary differences using a higher salary from a different position within the company, inflating the amount by 14,068,174 CFA francs.

This alleged mechanism is not an isolated incident, but a sustained practice to inflate amounts companies must deposit in judicial proceedings, according to a vice president. If confirmed, this scheme could allow judicial bodies to benefit financially regardless of the appeal's outcome, posing a risk to companies operating in Equatorial Guinea, particularly those in the oil sector.

gq.headline: DRC Opposition Urges President Tshisekedi to Halt Constitutional Changes
gq.dek: The C64 opposition coalition in the Democratic Republic of Congo is pressing President Tshisekedi to abandon constitutional reforms that could extend his term beyond 2028.
paragraphs: Delly Sesanga, president of the ENVOL party and a member of the C64 opposition coalition, stated that the opposition's priority is to ensure President Tshisekedi leaves office at the end of his second and final term in 2028. Tshisekedi, who has been in power since 2019, secured a second five-year term in the 2023 elections, and the current constitution prohibits him from seeking another term.

The debate over constitutional reform unfolds as the country continues to face conflicts, particularly in the east. The M23 armed group, reportedly backed by Rwanda, controls significant areas of North and South Kivu, contributing to ongoing instability. Sesanga claims that neither the government nor the armed group can achieve a decisive military victory.

Sesanga emphasized the need for an inclusive political process to address the country's security and economic crises, alongside calling for an end to hostilities. With elections scheduled for 2028, the opposition aims to increase pressure against any constitutional changes that would allow the president to prolong his stay in power.

gq.headline: ANIF receives training from Guatemala's IVE to improve financial crime prevention
gq.dek: Equatorial Guinea's National Financial Intelligence Agency (ANIF) is undergoing training from Guatemala's IVE to strengthen its capabilities against money laundering and.
paragraphs: The ANIF is receiving training from specialists of Guatemala's IVE, which began today and will continue until August twenty-seventh. This initiative aims to enhance the national system for preventing and combating money laundering, terrorism financing, and the financing of weapons of mass destruction proliferation, addressing recommendations from the Mutual Evaluation Report of the Central African Anti-Money Laundering Group (GABAC) and the National Action Plan.

Zenón Obiang Obiang Avomo, ANIF's national director, highlighted the importance of cooperation between similar institutions and the exchange of experiences within the Egmont Group. He emphasized that the evolving financial crime risks necessitate well-trained personnel, effective coordination mechanisms, and the ability to respond to new scenarios. The director also stressed the need to apply acquired knowledge to identify areas for improvement and implement concrete measures.

Milagrosa Obono Angüe, Minister Delegate of Finance, Budgets, and National Planning, underscored that this training is a priority within the National Action Plan and the GABAC mutual evaluation process. She emphasized the need for a cooperative structure extending beyond the Financial Intelligence Unit, involving public institutions, financial entities, and other actors to ensure the system's effectiveness in detecting financial crimes.

gq.headline: Education Ministry intensifies inspections of Malabo school renovations
gq.dek: The Ministry of Education is increasing oversight of rehabilitation projects at 46 schools in Malabo and Bata to ensure quality standards are met before the 2026-2027 school year.
paragraphs: Constantino Obiang Esono Ayingono, the Delegate Minister of Education, responsible for School and Sports Infrastructure, continued inspections of educational centers undergoing rehabilitation in Malabo. Accompanied by inspectors from GE Proyectos and regional education officials, the minister verified the progress and adherence to government standards at several schools.

During the inspections, Obiang Esono Ayingono visited the Cuartel Mañe Ela National School and Siale Bileka National School, where Lea Multiservicios is performing work. He also supervised projects at Bioko Norte National School by MS, and Cuartel Sipopo de Marina National School and 3 de Agosto de la Presidencia School, managed by VIKO S.L. Companies presented their advancements at each site.

The minister emphasized the need for serious, responsible work that meets established quality standards. This initiative is part of a national plan to improve educational infrastructure and provide suitable learning environments for students. Inspections will extend to the Continental Region for other schools in the program.

er.headline: Eritrean Embassy refutes tanker hijacking claims, clarifies flag status
er.dek: The Eritrean Embassy in London has denied reports of an "Eritrean flagged" oil tanker being hijacked off Yemen, stating the vessel has no ties to Eritrea.
paragraphs: The Embassy of the State of Eritrea in London clarified today that reports from news outlets, including Reuters, AFP, and BBC, about a hijacked "Eritrean flagged" oil tanker on August 20, 2026, are inaccurate. The Embassy stated that the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO), cited as the primary source, did not mention the ship being Eritrean flagged in its report, a fact UKMTO reiterated to the Embassy.

Further investigation by the Eritrean Embassy revealed that the ship, identified by IMO Registration 920476, is not owned by or linked to Eritrea. The International Maritime Organization (IMO) categorizes this vessel as part of a "Shadow Fleet" with "indeterminate ownership." Eritrea's Permanent Mission to the IMO confirmed that official records show the ship is "flying a false Eritrean flag; i.e. as not owned or officially registered in Eritrea."

The Embassy criticized what it called a "despicable campaign of disinformation on Eritrea," asserting that the true facts contradict the initial media reports. This clarification aims to correct the record regarding the vessel's nationality and ownership, emphasizing that the ship has no official connection to the State of Eritrea.

er.headline: Eritrea celebrates Eid Mewlid Al-Nebi nationwide
er.dek: The 1448 Hijri year's Eid Mewlid Al-Nebi was celebrated across Eritrea today, with a main ceremony in Asmara attended by government officials and religious leaders.
paragraphs: Eritrea marked Eid Mewlid Al-Nebi, commemorating the 1448 Hijri year, with nationwide celebrations today, August 25. The main ceremony took place at the Al-Khulafa Al-Rashidin Mosque in Asmara, drawing a large congregation of faithful alongside ministers, senior Government and PFDJ officials, members of the diplomatic community, and leaders from various Churches.

Haj Mohammed-Seid Bashir, Chairman of the Islamic Awkaf of Asmara, provided a detailed briefing on the historical importance of the holiday and acknowledged those who contributed to the event. Sheik Salem Ibrahim Almuktar, Mufti of Eritrea and Chairman of the Higher Assembly of Eritrean Iftae and Islamic Affairs, extended congratulations to Eritreans both within the country and abroad.

Sheik Salem Ibrahim Almuktar emphasized the continued importance of adhering to Eritrea’s foundational ethical principles and standards amidst globalization. He also called for the preservation and strengthening of the nation's strong national unity and cohesion, which he stated were secured through the sacrifices of its martyrs. The celebration featured spiritual performances.

er.headline: Eritrea expands renewable energy supply and use
er.dek: The Ministry of Energy and Mines is working to increase the availability and adoption of renewable energy sources across Eritrea, including solar, wind, and bioenergy.
paragraphs: Eritrea is expanding its renewable energy infrastructure, with the Ministry of Energy and Mines reporting encouraging results from efforts to introduce and expand various clean energy sources. Mr. Tesfay Gebrehiwet, Director of Renewable Energy at the Ministry, noted that these initiatives cover household, agricultural, and other purposes, encompassing solar, wind, geothermal, green-hydrogen, and bioenergy technologies.

Significant progress has been made in solar energy, with 34 megawatts installed in Dekemhare, 2 megawatts around Asmara, and 2.25 megawatts in Areza and Mai-Dima. The Ministry is also organizing training for producers of smokeless ovens and other household appliances, building on a Ministry of Agriculture initiative from 2000 that has seen approximately 200,000 beneficiaries adopt these ovens.

To support this expansion, theoretical and practical capacity-building training has been provided by both foreign and national experts, with ongoing efforts planned. Mr. Tesfay also called for greater public understanding of solar energy systems and their proper use to maximize the benefits of these renewable energy projects.

er.headline: Eritrean Officials Conduct Seminar to Eradicate Harmful Practices
er.dek: A three-day seminar in Assab gathered representatives from justice, police, and social services to address harmful practices like underage marriage and female genital mutilation.
paragraphs: A seminar focused on eradicating harmful practices concluded on August twenty-first in Assab, Southern Red Sea Region. The event, which ran from August nineteenth, brought together partner institutions including the Ministry of Justice, police, social service institutions, and reconciliation committees.

The seminar was organized through a collaboration between the Ministry of Labor and Social Welfare, the Ministry of Health, and the National Union of Eritrean Women branch in the region. Discussions covered women’s and children’s rights, public registration, traditional values, case resolution, legal perspectives on harmful practices, and the consequences of female genital mutilation.

The primary objective was to improve public understanding and participation in efforts to eliminate practices such as underage marriage and female genital mutilation. Ambassador Mohammed Sid Mantai, Governor of the region, urged participants to take a leading role in these eradication efforts.

ke.headline: Police to Recommend Violent Political Actors to IEBC for Action
ke.dek: The National Police Service will submit names of individuals with a history of promoting political violence to the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission for.
paragraphs: The National Police Service (NPS) announced it will recommend individuals deemed unfit to contest elective positions to the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) based on their record of promoting or perpetrating political violence. Deputy Inspector General Gilbert Masengeli stated that security agencies are intensifying efforts to prevent politically instigated violence ahead of the 2027 General Election.

This decision follows a recent incident on August 16 where violence disrupted a political rally in Homa Bay County, leading to the arrest of 37 suspected gang members found with crude weapons. During the incident, one police officer died and eight others were injured, including three injured the previous day during arrests along the Kisumu-Kericho Road.

Masengeli, speaking at the launch of the Roadmap to a Peaceful General Election 2027, warned that individuals involved in organizing or sponsoring violence would face firm action. The NPS is pursuing organizers, facilitators, and sponsors of criminal activities, emphasizing investigations, arrests, and crime prevention as key responses.

ke.dek: Policymakers, scientists, investors, and entrepreneurs at the Africa Bioeconomy Workshop in Nairobi called for linking agricultural production, research, and innovation to markets.
paragraphs: Experts at the Africa Bioeconomy Workshop in Nairobi are pushing East Africa to transition from bioeconomy research to building profitable industries. The call emphasizes creating jobs and retaining more value from the region’s biological resources, moving beyond exporting raw materials.

Niall O’Connor, Centre Director of the Stockholm Environment Institute (SEI) Africa Centre, stated that the region possesses the necessary resources, research capacity, and entrepreneurial talent to establish a competitive bio-based economy. The 2026 State of the Bioeconomy in Eastern Africa report identifies agricultural residues and organic waste as potential feedstock for various industries.

Dr. Abdou Tenkouano, Director General of the International Centre of Insect Physiology and Ecology (icipe), highlighted agriculture's significant contribution of between 23 and 35 percent of GDP in many sub-Saharan African countries as a major opportunity. He urged governments to strengthen university-industry partnerships to promote innovation and entrepreneurship in agro-processing and bioprocessing.

ke.headline: Mombasa Court Acquits Clinical Officer in Patient Rape Case
ke.dek: A Mombasa court acquitted a former Pandya Memorial Hospital clinical officer accused of raping a dialysis patient, citing insufficient evidence to prove the case beyond.
paragraphs: Chief Magistrate Lucas Onyina found Dias Juma Wabwile not guilty of rape and an alternative charge of committing an indecent act. Wabwile was accused of unlawfully penetrating an adult patient, identified as M.T.K., at Pandya Memorial Hospital in Mvita Sub-County around five am on January thirty-one, two thousand twenty-five. The complainant died before the hearing began, and no witnesses observed the alleged assault.

The case involved a used condom found in a hospital dustbin, which government analysis confirmed contained Wabwile’s DNA. Wabwile admitted the condom was his, claiming he had sex with his wife at home before work and brought the used condom to the hospital for disposal. His wife, Nancy Gakii, supported this account, stating they had sex at about three thirty am that morning.

The magistrate questioned Wabwile’s explanation about wrapping the condom in tissue and how the complainant knew where it was discarded. The court noted the patient was connected to a dialysis machine, making disconnection risky, and inferred that Wabwile might have taken advantage of the situation. However, the court stressed this was an inference, not proof, and consent could not be presumed without the complainant's testimony.

ke.headline: Nairobi designer revives traditional hand looms for clothing production
ke.dek: Hillary Mukubwa, founder of Mukabwa studios, uses hand looms to create unique clothing and fabrics, moving away from mass production trends.
paragraphs: In Nairobi, designer Hillary Mukubwa is reintroducing traditional hand looms for clothing production, a departure from modern mass production methods. Mukubwa, who founded Mukabwa studios, stated that he aims to revive old practices where culture lives, viewing hand looms as a way to keep Kenya's cultural heritage alive.

Mukubwa explained that hand looms are traditional and carry a story, producing items with meaning rather than in mass quantities. He feels like an anomaly in returning to these older traditions, noting that modernization often diminishes traditional craftsmanship.

Clients appreciate the individuality and quality of the clothes, which are made from organic cotton. Maylone Ginnette, a client, highlighted the uniqueness of the pieces and the visible effort involved in their creation, preferring them over high street offerings.

ke.headline: Kenyan anime fans transform recycled materials into cosplay culture
ke.dek: Over 4,000 anime and manga enthusiasts gathered in Nairobi for the Otamatsuri convention, showcasing elaborate costumes crafted from unconventional materials.
paragraphs: Thousands of anime and manga fans in Nairobi recently transformed recycled materials and craft skills into elaborate costumes for one of Africa’s largest cosplay conventions. The Otamatsuri event, which attracted more than 4,000 attendees, highlights the growing popularity of Japanese pop culture in Kenya, according to organizer Jotham Micah.

For many Kenyan cosplayers, creating these detailed costumes involves finding affordable and unconventional materials. Julius Mokaya, a 34-year-old building caretaker and two-time winner of the convention's costume competition, uses cardboard and other items collected from recycling bins to craft his outfits, as he cannot afford to import expensive costumes.

Micah, co-founder of entertainment company Movie Jabber, stated that anime and manga are increasingly crossing cultural boundaries, providing inspiration and entertainment. The convention featured fans dressed as characters from popular Japanese franchises like One Piece, Naruto, and Gachiakuta, demonstrating a space for creativity, friendship, and self-expression.

za.headline: Police arrest four suspects in Zolani Tete murder investigation
za.dek: Eastern Cape police have arrested three additional suspects, bringing the total to four, in connection with the killing of former boxing world champion Zolani Tete.
paragraphs: South African police have arrested four individuals in connection with the murder of former two-division boxing world champion Zolani Tete. The arrests follow the shooting death of Tete outside his home in Mdantsane on Friday, 21 August. One suspect is scheduled to appear in court on Monday to face charges of murder and attempted murder, according to Africanews and BBC Africa.

Tete, born on 8 March 1988 in Mdantsane, was a celebrated boxer known for his power and precision. He turned professional in 2006 and achieved world titles, including the IBF junior-bantamweight title in 2014 and the WBO bantamweight title in 2017. His career included 29 wins out of 34 professional fights, with 22 knockouts.

A notable moment in Tete's career was his 11-second knockout of Siboniso Gonya in November 2017, setting a Guinness World Record for the fastest knockout in a world title fight. Despite a four-year suspension in 2022 for a banned substance, Tete was preparing for a comeback when his suspension was set to end in July 2026.

za.headline: Supreme Court hears government appeal on R370 grant legality
za.dek: The Supreme Court of Appeal in Bloemfontein is reviewing a High Court ruling that found aspects of South Africa's R370 Social Relief of Distress (SRD) grant system unlawful.
paragraphs: The South African government is challenging a January 2025 High Court judgment that declared several regulations governing the SRD grant unconstitutional, arguing that the High Court overstepped its powers by effectively making a temporary intervention permanent. The High Court had found that administrative requirements, such as online-only applications, unfairly restricted access for vulnerable people without reliable internet access.

The case, brought by the Institute for Economic Justice (IEJ) and #PayTheGrants, also scrutinizes the R370 grant amount and the R624 monthly means-test threshold. The High Court had ordered the government to develop a plan to progressively increase both, noting that the R370 grant falls short of the R855 food poverty line.

The government maintains the SRD grant was a temporary Covid-19 measure and disputes that online applications are inherently exclusionary, citing over 15 million applications and 8.7 million paid beneficiaries through the digital platform. National Treasury has expressed concerns about the financial implications if the High Court ruling is upheld, while activists point to a 33% database error rate and a 99% appeal rejection rate as evidence of a broken system.
