za.headline: US National Institutes of Health lifts South Africa funding ban
za.dek: The US National Institutes of Health has reversed its nearly 18-month ban on South Africa, allowing funding for "meritorious research projects" to resume.
paragraphs: The US National Institutes of Health (NIH) has lifted its ban on South Africa, which had halted many clinical trials and led to the retrenchment of numerous researchers. The decision comes after 12 months of negotiations between the NIH and the South African Medical Research Council (SAMRC), according to SAMRC president and CEO Ntobeko Ntusi.

An internal memo dated August seventeen, signed by NIH director Jay Bhattacharya, confirmed the lifting of the ban, stating that funding for research projects in South Africa may now proceed. The memo, marked "Not for distribution outside government," clarifies that NIH grants are distinct from traditional foreign aid.

The ban, initiated in February, had created a crisis for HIV and TB research in South Africa, impacting critical research initiatives and decades of investment in research infrastructure. Research in South Africa, often led by local scientists with NIH funding, has historically shaped global health policies for TB and HIV prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and care.

za.headline: Ramaphosa defends municipal governance, claims end to load shedding
za.dek: President Cyril Ramaphosa addressed concerns about municipal failures and asserted the ANC's role in ending load shedding, 70 days before local government elections.
paragraphs: President Cyril Ramaphosa defended his administration's efforts to improve municipal governance and the national water action plan during a virtual presidential question time. He foreshadowed "far-reaching reforms" to rebuild trust and foster inclusive economic growth for municipalities, citing the near completion of the local government white paper review.

Ramaphosa also claimed the African National Congress (ANC) deserved credit for ending load shedding, stating the country has recorded 460 consecutive days without it. Speaking at the ANC's manifesto delivery in Diepsloot, Gauteng, he attributed this to effective leadership and cooperation, while acknowledging ongoing load reduction in some areas.

Democratic Alliance parliamentary leader George Michalakis challenged Ramaphosa on the ANC's management of municipalities, specifically citing water delivery failures like 65% water losses in eThekwini. Ramaphosa responded by emphasizing the need for partnerships and practical plans from all parties to address these issues.

za.headline: Women leaders discuss power, legacy seventy years after Union Buildings march
za.dek: Seventy years after more than 20 000 women marched to the Union Buildings, women leaders reflected on progress and persistent challenges in achieving real power.
paragraphs: A Women's Month conversation, "From the Union Buildings to the Boardroom," brought together women leaders from different generations to discuss the journey from gaining access to exercising real power. The event, hosted by A Seat At The Table Connect Board Mastery, highlighted that while much has changed since 1956, getting women into leadership roles is only part of the ongoing work.

The host emphasized the responsibility of those who were "first" in their families to attend university, enter corporate South Africa, become executives, or start businesses. She stated that being the first should entail ensuring others do not have to fight the same battles alone, underscoring the theme of passing on knowledge and support.

Former minister Ayanda Dlodlo delivered the keynote address, remembering women whose stories are often overlooked in leadership discussions. Dlodlo, who grew up in Soweto and lived in exile, dedicated her address to women and a man from her unit killed in Piet Retief in 1988, and a friend assassinated in Eswatini, stressing the need to continue telling these stories of resilience and leadership.

ng.headline: PDP Candidate Archibong Accepts Governor Otu's Debate Challenge for 2027 Election
ng.dek: Arthur Archibong, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Cross River, has agreed to debate Governor Bassey Otu ahead of the 2027 election.
paragraphs: Archibong stated his readiness to debate Governor Otu at any time and venue the governor chooses, provided Otu attends personally. This acceptance comes in response to a challenge issued by the state Commissioner for Information, Ekpenyong Cobham, who had called for a public debate on the Otu administration's policies and performance.

The PDP candidate emphasized that the public deserves to hear directly from those seeking to lead them, not from proxies. He declined to engage Cobham in a war of words, noting that the commissioner is not on the ballot. Archibong also defended Arthur Jarvis University, which he founded, against what he described as politically motivated criticisms.

Archibong raised concerns about environmental sanitation, blocked drainages, and the condition of Watt Market, urging critics to focus on these issues. He also alleged inadequate resources for emergency response, citing a lack of diesel for fire trucks and water for firefighters, and questioned the economic benefits of the administration's foreign investment trips.

ng.headline: Refineries increase crude imports by 151.5% in July
ng.dek: Domestic refineries imported 5.13 million barrels of crude oil in July 2026, a significant rise from 2.04 million barrels in June, according to the NMDPRA.
paragraphs: Crude oil imports by domestic refineries increased by 151.5 per cent to 5.13 million barrels in July 2026, up from 2.04 million barrels in June. This increase occurred as the domestic supply of crude to refineries declined during the same period, according to data from the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA).

The NMDPRA’s July 2026 Midstream and Downstream Statistics report indicated that domestic refineries received a total of 17.88 million barrels of crude in July. Of this, 12.75 million barrels were supplied locally, while 5.13 million barrels were imported. Imported crude accounted for 28.7 per cent of total crude receipts, with domestic supplies making up 71.3 per cent.

The 5.13 million barrels imported in July marked a substantial increase from the 2.04 million barrels in June and 2.08 million barrels in May. However, this volume remained below the 9.43 million barrels recorded in March, which was the highest monthly import volume in 2026. The Dangote Refinery operated at an average capacity utilisation of 71.09 per cent in July.

ng.headline: Nigeria's new health policy improves doctor working conditions and patient care
ng.dek: The National Health Sector Reform Initiative II (NHSRII) aims to ensure doctors are rested after shifts and locum employees receive clear contracts and regular pay.
paragraphs: Nigeria's new health policy, the NHSRII, intends to improve health outcomes by ensuring doctors can finish a call, hand over to a rested colleague, and go home. This initiative addresses the working conditions of medical professionals, aiming for a more sustainable and effective healthcare system.

Under the new policy, locum employees are expected to have clear contracts, receive regular pay, and transition away from temporary status. This change seeks to provide greater stability and fairness for doctors working in temporary capacities, ensuring they are properly integrated into the healthcare workforce.

The ultimate goal of the NHSRII is for patients to be treated by properly staffed teams, rather than overworked individuals. This focus on adequate staffing and rested medical personnel is designed to enhance the quality and safety of patient care across the country, according to the Premium Times.

et.headline: Excavator bucket kills six in Addis Ababa minibus crash
et.dek: A traffic accident in Addis Ababa on Monday, August 24, claimed the lives of at least six people when an excavator's bucket fell onto a moving minibus taxi.
paragraphs: At least six people died in Ethiopia's capital, Addis Ababa, on Monday, August 24, after an excavator bucket struck a minibus taxi in the Bole Subcity. The Addis Ababa Police reported that the incident occurred in the morning, resulting in the immediate deaths of six passengers.

The driver and several other passengers aboard the minibus sustained injuries, ranging from serious to minor, and were transported to nearby health facilities for treatment. Police have initiated an investigation to determine the precise cause of the accident, according to a statement issued Monday.

This incident adds to a series of fatal traffic accidents in the East African nation, which authorities often link to factors such as reckless driving, inadequate law enforcement, and poor vehicle conditions. Experts are calling for stricter safety enforcement, thorough vehicle inspections, and more rigorous licensing systems to prevent future tragedies as vehicle numbers increase with economic growth and an expanding middle class.

et.headline: Ethiopia bids to host 2028 Africa Cup of Nations
et.dek: Ethiopia has submitted an official bid to host the 2028 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon), aiming to bring the tournament back for the first time in over 50 years.
paragraphs: Ethiopia's football federation (EFF) has submitted a government-backed proposal to host the 2028 Africa Cup of Nations, affirming the nation's readiness for Africa's largest football event. The country last hosted Afcon in 1976 and has only qualified three times since then, most recently for the delayed 2021 edition.

The bid comes despite Ethiopia's current football infrastructure lagging behind other African nations. Last season, only one stadium was approved by the Confederation of African Football (Caf) for use. However, a new international stadium and sports complex in Addis Ababa is being inaugurated, which could serve as a venue.

A key challenge for Ethiopia will be providing enough compliant venues for a 24-team Afcon across multiple locations, as many existing regional facilities do not meet Fifa or Caf standards for infrastructure and match-day requirements. Ethiopia played its home qualifiers for the 2026 Fifa World Cup at neutral venues in Morocco and Rwanda, though it did host matches in Dire Dawa earlier this year, according to BBC Africa and Africanews reports.

et.headline: WHO, AU Leaders Urge African Health Sovereignty
et.dek: Leaders from the World Health Organization and African Union called for Africa to achieve health self-reliance and reduce dependence on external financing.
paragraphs: The 76th Session of the WHO Regional Committee for Africa, held in Addis Ababa, brought together African health ministers and leaders of regional and international health institutions. Mohamed Yakub Janabi, WHO regional director for Africa, stated that the session will review Africa’s determination to shape its own health future and make decisions and recommendations to improve health services across the continent.

This initiative aims to reduce the nearly 7 billion U.S. dollars the continent spends annually on referring patients abroad. Janabi emphasized strengthening Africa’s centers of excellence, connecting African patients to African expertise, and keeping investments working for Africa. He noted that African countries have improved surveillance systems, expanded access to essential health services, and responded to outbreaks with growing speed.

AU Commission Chairperson Mahmoud Ali Youssouf highlighted Africa's efforts to create conditions for health sovereignty through vaccine production and increased budgets to strengthen collective capacity against health threats. Ethiopian President Taye Atske Selassie, the guest of honor, added that climate change and conflict exert pressure on communities, offering an opportunity for Africa to deepen regional cooperation and assume full ownership of its health architecture.

et.headline: Ethiopian Consumers Face 15.3% Annual Price Increase in July
et.dek: Ethiopia's headline inflation reached 15.3% in July, driven by rising fuel and food costs, marking the highest rate since January 2025.
paragraphs: Ethiopia's Consumer Price Index (CPI) climbed 2.6% in July, pushing the annual inflation rate to 15.3%, according to data from the Ethiopian Statistical Service (ESS). This increase, which is the highest since January 2025, follows a 13.9% gain in June and aligns with the National Bank of Ethiopia's projection that inflation will remain in double-digits.

Non-food inflation accelerated by 3.0% for the month and 14.8% annually, matching the highest rate recorded in September 2025. Education services saw a 25.3% annual surge, while transport costs rose 15.6% year-on-year, indicating that higher fuel prices are affecting other sectors. Housing, water, electricity, gas, and other fuels, the largest component of non-food CPI, increased by 3.3% monthly and 13.3% annually.

Food inflation also contributed significantly, reaching an annual rate of 15.7%, the highest since January 2025, with a monthly increase of 2.3%. Sugar, jam, and honey prices surged 39.4% annually, while non-alcoholic beverages and coffee rose 33%. Meat prices saw the largest monthly gain at 4.4%, and bread and cereals, the largest food CPI component, increased 1.4% monthly and 8.0% annually.

Students can access their results through various platforms, including the EAES website, Telegram, and short text messages. This digital distribution aims to provide broad access for all examinees across the country.

gh.headline: Ghana Study Finds Oranges, Sardines Reduce Air Pollution Symptoms
gh.dek: A new Ghanaian study suggests that a diet rich in oranges, peanuts, sunflower oil, eggs, and sardines can help street vendors in Accra mitigate health issues caused by prolonged.
paragraphs: Researchers from the University of Cape Coast found that street vendors who consumed specific antioxidant-rich foods reported fewer symptoms associated with air pollution. The study, led by Professor Kofi Amegah, followed 307 vendors in Accra for 12 months, with one group receiving a weekly supply of these foods while a control group maintained their usual diets.

The findings indicate significant reductions in health complaints among the intervention group. They were 55 percent less likely to develop a persistent cough, 60 percent less likely to experience difficulty breathing, and 81 percent less likely to suffer dizziness. The most notable difference was an 92 percent reduction in irregular heartbeat, and a 66 percent decrease in hospital admissions for the studied symptoms.

The study focused on vendors working along Accra's busiest roads, including Atomic Junction, Madina, and Kwame Nkrumah Circle, where air quality monitors recorded average PM2.5 levels of about 40 micrograms per cubic meter, exceeding the World Health Organization's recommended 15 micrograms per cubic meter. Professor Amegah noted that the biological basis for these results is that antioxidants help neutralize pollutants.

gh.headline: DirectAid distributes GH¢2 million in flood relief to 1,500 families
gh.dek: Humanitarian organization DirectAid began distributing food and household items to residents of Alajo, Accra, as part of a GH¢2 million relief program for June 2026 flood victims.
paragraphs: DirectAid started distributing relief items to flood-affected residents in Alajo, Accra, on Tuesday, August 25. This initiative is part of a larger GH¢2 million program designed to support approximately 1,500 families across five communities impacted by the June 2026 floods. Beneficiaries in Alajo received packages containing rice, cooking oil, spaghetti, beans, tomatoes, mattresses, bedsheets, blankets, towels, and cleaning products.

Sami Henedak Ahmed, Country Director of DirectAid, stated that the intervention aims to support families whose homes and livelihoods were affected by the June floods. The relief items were provided through the support of DirectAid’s donors in Kuwait, with assistance from government officials coordinating the exercise. The organization also plans to extend support to clinics and hospitals by donating medical supplies.

The distribution will continue in Alogboshie on Wednesday, Kasoa on Thursday, and Nana Krom on Saturday, concluding next week with a final distribution in Abeka. The June 2026 floods resulted in the loss of many lives and destroyed property valued at millions, affecting nearly 92,000 people and killing 39, according to Muntaka.

gh.headline: US Judge Rejects Ghislaine Maxwell's Conviction Appeal
gh.dek: A U.S. judge dismissed Ghislaine Maxwell's attempt to overturn her conviction and 20-year prison sentence for assisting Jeffrey Epstein in sex abuse.
paragraphs: U.S. District Judge Paul Engelmayer in Manhattan rejected Ghislaine Maxwell’s claims as meritless, stating that most were frivolous or based on arguments previously lost. Maxwell, who represented herself, sought a writ of habeas corpus to declare her punishment unlawful, arguing that new evidence from the Epstein Files Transparency Act was relevant.

Judge Engelmayer’s 67-page decision, made public on Tuesday, stated that any relevant new evidence incriminates Maxwell or reinforces the correctness of prior legal rulings. He also called her claim that prosecutors illegally withheld evidence "conclusory, cynical, and wrong." Prosecutors had argued Maxwell’s latest claims were baseless, filed too late, or failed to show her trial was unfair.

Maxwell had also asserted that lawyers for Epstein’s accusers acted as “De Facto Prosecutors” and that prosecutors did not conduct their own investigations. Jurors convicted Maxwell on five charges for recruiting and grooming underage girls for Epstein between 1994 and 2004. She is currently housed at a minimum-security federal prison camp in Bryan, Texas.

gh.headline: Gold Fields flags Ghana license risk as half-year profit surges
gh.dek: Uncertainty over the renewal of Gold Fields’ mining leases in Ghana is weighing on the company’s valuation, despite an 81% jump in half-year profit.
paragraphs: Gold Fields reported an 81% increase in half-year profit, driven by higher gold prices and output, but its CEO Mike Fraser stated that the uncertainty surrounding the renewal of its Tarkwa mine leases in Ghana is affecting investor valuation. The leases are set to expire in April 2027, and the company has not yet received a formal response to its renewal application submitted in November 2025.

Fraser indicated that the market has largely discounted the Tarkwa asset in Gold Fields’ portfolio, causing its shares to trade at a discount compared to peers. He emphasized that an early resolution would benefit all parties involved, noting that there are "a lot of influences" in the decision-making process without further elaboration.

The company is considering all available options, including exercising its legal rights under the leases, which Fraser described as a last resort to protect shareholder value. Ghana’s Minerals Commission CEO, Isaac Andrews Tandoh, denied in May that the government was delaying renewals, stating that Gold Fields must present its development plans for review.

gh.headline: Ghana Maritime Authority commissions 4 boreholes, improving student attendance in Wa
gh.dek: The Ghana Maritime Authority and Humanity First Ghana have installed four solar-powered boreholes in Wa, ending water scarcity and reducing school disruptions for students.

These facilities, located at T.I. Ahmadiyya Senior High School, Chansa, Biihee, and Boli, are part of a larger seven-borehole Corporate Social Responsibility initiative aimed at addressing severe water distress and improving public sanitation across the Upper West Region.

Naval Captain (Rtd) Dr. Kamal-Deen Ali, Director General of the GMA, stated that the intervention aligns with national development priorities to provide clean, potable water to underserved communities. He emphasized that bringing these facilities directly to schools and communities prevents pupils and students from leaving premises to search for water, thereby protecting instructional hours and enhancing their studies.

The new boreholes have brought immediate relief to beneficiary schools. At T.I. Ahmadiyya Senior High School, Headmaster Issahaque Yahaya noted that reliable water helps manage sanitation for 1,433 students. Students reported a decrease in typhoid cases and improved hygiene routines, while at Boli M/A Primary B, Headteacher Osman Issah confirmed that pupils no longer leave school during instructional periods to fetch water.

paragraphs: The health zone of Popokabaka is experiencing a resurgence of cholera, with Médecins sans frontières (MSF) epidemiological services reporting 756 cases and 27 fatalities. These figures, released on Monday, August 24, cover the period from June 1 to August 24, 2026.

MSF teams are collaborating with local health personnel to manage the epidemic. Their efforts include supplying care, treating patients, and providing support to the teams involved in the response to the outbreak in the Kwango province.

cd.headline: Grand Tambour Nears Two-Year Mark, Raises Operational Questions
cd.dek: The Centre Culturel et artistique pour les pays de l’Afrique centrale, known as Grand Tambour, approaches its second anniversary with questions about its full operational status.
paragraphs: The Grand Tambour, inaugurated on December fourteen, two thousand twenty-four, is nearing two years of existence. This cultural complex, located in Kasa-Vubu commune opposite the Palais du Peuple, spans some ninety-three thousand square meters and was opened by President Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi.

The facility includes a two thousand-seat performance hall, an eight hundred-seat amphitheater, recording studios, a dance hall, and accommodation rooms. It also houses the campus of the National Institute of Arts (INA), aiming to foster artistic creation, training, and cultural promotion for the Democratic Republic of Congo and Central Africa.

Despite its ambitious goals and extensive infrastructure, questions remain regarding whether the center's facilities are fully operational and accessible, and if it meets the expectations of artists and the public nearly two years after its opening, according to Radio Okapi.

tz.headline: Dr Magembe joins Tanzanian delegation at WHO Africa session
tz.dek: Tanzania's Chief Medical Officer, Dr Grace Magembe, has arrived in Addis Ababa to participate in the 76th Session of the WHO Regional Committee for Africa.
paragraphs: Dr Grace Magembe, Tanzania’s Chief Medical Officer and Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Health, joined the Tanzanian delegation in Addis Ababa for the 76th Session of the World Health Organization (WHO) Regional Committee for Africa. The meeting, which runs from August 25 to 28, 2026, focuses on strengthening health systems and sharing experiences among African nations. Dr Magembe was welcomed by Tanzania’s Ambassador to Ethiopia, Innocent Shiyo, and other officials.

The Tanzanian delegation, led by Deputy Minister for Health, Dr Florence Samizi, will engage in discussions aimed at improving health service delivery across the continent. Dr Magembe is also scheduled to attend various side meetings and activities centered on health and international cooperation, facilitating the exchange of strategies.

Tanzania's participation underscores its role in advancing Africa’s health agenda, particularly in maternal, child, and reproductive health. This commitment aligns with President Dr Samia Suluhu Hassan's position as the African Union (AU) Champion for Maternal and Child Health, reflecting the nation's dedication to promoting the well-being of women and children in Africa.

tz.headline: Tanzania Vice President Nchimbi resigns from office
tz.dek: Emmanuel Nchimbi announced his resignation from politics and public service today, effective September four, 2026, making him the first vice-president to quit since independence.
paragraphs: Tanzanian Vice President Emmanuel Nchimbi tendered his resignation today, August 25, 2026, through his Instagram account, which the Chief Secretary confirmed President Samia Suluhu Hassan has accepted. Nchimbi stated he is retiring from politics and public service, with his resignation from the Vice Presidency effective September four, 2026.

The resignation follows reports of a rift between Nchimbi and President Hassan, which escalated after Nchimbi's July 24, 2026, speech urging the public to “fight for the new constitution.” He was also summoned before the party’s ethics committee on July 29, 2026, following a proposal by a Cabinet minister.

Nchimbi's announcement on an account he last used in 2023 surprised many, as he had not used it for official communications before. Political analyst William Maduhu noted that if Nchimbi were expelled from his political party, his position as Vice President would automatically become vacant, as a member of a political party is a qualification for the office.

tz.headline: Tanzania advances Lake Victoria investments to boost economy, regional integration
tz.dek: The Permanent Secretary for East African affairs, Charles Ngeleja Kadonya, highlighted the Lake Victoria Basin's strategic role in economic growth and EAC integration.
paragraphs: Tanzania is actively pursuing investments in the Lake Victoria Basin to enhance its economy and strengthen regional integration within the East African Community (EAC). Charles Ngeleja Kadonya, Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and East African Cooperation, emphasized the lake's potential for trade, investment, transportation, and resource utilization during a tour in Mwanza.

Kadonya stressed that these projects must directly benefit citizens by creating employment, increasing incomes, and reducing poverty. He also underlined the importance of enabling Tanzanians to participate fully in these investments to become part of the value chain and benefit from the lake's resources.

During his visit, Kadonya inspected the MV Mwanza – Hapa Kazi Tu vessel, rescue boats, and a rehabilitated research vessel used for fish stock and water quality studies. Mwanza Regional Commissioner Said Mtanda noted ongoing government investments in strategic projects, including Mwanza Airport upgrades and port infrastructure, to strengthen the region's economy.

tz.headline: Tanzania seeks global investment to restore degraded land
tz.dek: Tanzania has called on the international community to increase investment, technology, and financial resources to combat desertification and land degradation.
paragraphs: Tanzania urged the international community to boost investment and financial resources for land restoration and to counter desertification, according to Hamad Masauni, Minister of State in the Vice President's Office (Union and Environment). The minister emphasized the need to protect grazing areas, forests, and water sources during the 17th Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD COP17), which opened in Ulaanbaatar.

Masauni stated that the conference, themed “Restore Land, Restore Hope,” focuses on increasing investment in land restoration, building resilience against drought, and sustainably managing grazing lands. He noted that the declaration of two thousand twenty-six as the International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists strengthens Tanzania's agenda for conserving grazing areas and improving pastoralist communities' well-being.

According to Thimoth Mande, Tanzania's National Coordinator for the Convention, international cooperation is crucial for the country to address land degradation, biodiversity loss, and climate change comprehensively. Tanzania's participation in the conference allows it to showcase ongoing efforts and seek further investment and technology, potentially leveraging resources from organizations like the Global Environment Facility (GEF) and the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD).

tz.headline: Dk Kiruswa funds Lailupa classroom completion with Sh milioni 6
tz.dek: Member of Parliament Dk Steven Kiruswa contributed Sh milioni 6 from his personal funds to complete a preschool classroom in Lailupa, Longido district.
paragraphs: The community of Lailupa in Meirugoi village, Longido district, received Sh milioni 6 from MP Dk Steven Kiruswa to finalize construction of a preschool classroom. This contribution will cover the remaining costs for one door, six windows, sixty corrugated iron sheets, twenty desks, timber, and plastering work for the Sh milioni 12 project.

Local residents, including mothers, youth, and traditional leaders, had initiated the classroom construction after children were observed studying under a tree, exposed to rain or sun. The Lailupa Hamlet Chairman, Ndung’anak Mepukor, stated that families contributed money, sold livestock, and participated in digging foundations and carrying bricks to build the classroom.

Dk Kiruswa, who is also the Deputy Minister of Minerals, made the pledge during a visit to inspect development projects in the ward. He commended the community's efforts and promised to ensure the preschool is registered and staffed by a qualified teacher by January next year, replacing the current volunteer teacher without formal qualifications.

ma.headline: Morocco offers game developers grants up to MAD 3 million for production
ma.dek: Moroccan video game companies can receive up to MAD 3 million for pilot production and MAD 1 million for prototypes under a new innovation program.
paragraphs: Morocco's Industry and Trade Ministry has opened applications for grants up to MAD 3 million for video game pilot production and MAD 1 million for prototypes. This initiative, part of the Innovation Support Fund's fourth call for projects, aims to develop a regional video game industry hub through 2028.

The program, which can support up to 20 projects annually with a MAD 50 million budget, covers up to 70% of eligible prototype costs and 30% for pilot industrialization. Applications for the 2026 round close on October 15, with eligible spending counted from January 1.

Micro, small, and medium-sized gaming companies with pre-tax revenue not exceeding MAD 200 million in the previous two years are eligible. High-growth startups with a strategic partnership with a large Moroccan company can also apply, following a November 2025 agreement that expanded the fund to include gaming companies.

ma.headline: IFC, EOS Group launch €60 million facility for Morocco's bad debt market
ma.dek: The International Finance Corporation and German debt specialist EOS Group are preparing a €60 million facility to acquire troubled loans in Morocco, marking the entry of.
paragraphs: Morocco's market for troubled loans is set to attract its first international investors, with the International Finance Corporation (IFC) and German debt specialist EOS Group preparing a €60 million facility. This initiative, reported by Asharq Bloomberg, will target nonperforming loans held by Moroccan banks, covering individuals and companies of all sizes, as well as real estate assets taken over during debt recovery.

The facility, known as DARP NPL EOS Morocco, will see the IFC, the World Bank’s private-sector investment arm, and EOS each contribute up to €30 million. This move comes as Morocco progresses towards establishing a regulated secondary market for nonperforming loans, a system supervised by Bank Al-Maghrib, which could allow banks to convert distressed loans into cash more efficiently.

Morocco's nonperforming loans reached MAD 104.7 billion by the end of June, an increase of about 1.9% from a year earlier, according to Bank Al-Maghrib. The biggest surge in bad debt, around 15%, occurred in 2020 due to the Covid-19 pandemic and economic slowdown. A functioning secondary market is expected to free up funds for new lending and reduce pressure on bank balance sheets.

ma.headline: TAQA Morocco doubles investment despite revenue drop
ma.dek: TAQA Morocco increased its capital spending to MAD 515 million in the first half of the year, more than double the previous year, even as revenue fell by 5.4%.
paragraphs: TAQA Morocco's capital spending more than doubled to MAD 515 million in the first half of the year, up from MAD 210 million a year earlier, according to its financial update. This increase occurred despite a 5.4% drop in first-half revenue to MAD 5.09 billion, attributed to scheduled maintenance and an unfavorable dollar-dirham exchange rate.

The company's second-quarter investment reached MAD 466 million, with funds directed towards low-carbon development, an overhaul of Unit 3, and operating and maintenance projects. Plant availability decreased to 86.6% from 93.4% due to a planned 25-day minor overhaul of Unit 3 and an inspection of Unit 2.

TAQA Morocco is expanding into desalination, renewable energy, natural gas, and low-carbon water and energy transport. A restructuring approved on July 17 will organize its activities into specialized subsidiaries as it transitions to a holding-company model, while net debt declined 10.1% to MAD 4.62 billion through cash generation and repayments.

ma.headline: Morocco reaffirms ASEAN-Africa connectivity role
ma.dek: Morocco's ambassador to ASEAN, Redouane Houssaini, highlighted the country's vision for comprehensive connectivity, encompassing digital networks, financial flows, energy.
paragraphs: Morocco reaffirmed its role as a bridge between the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and Africa in connectivity, according to Ambassador Redouane Houssaini. Speaking at a meeting in Manila, Philippines, from August twenty-fourth to twenty-sixth, Houssaini emphasized that connectivity extends beyond physical infrastructure to include digital, financial, energy, and human links.

Houssaini cited projects like the Tanger Med port complex, which connects to over 180 ports in 70 countries, and the Royal Initiative for Sahel countries' access to the Atlantic Ocean, including Dakhla Atlantique, as examples of Morocco's efforts. He also mentioned the Nigeria-Morocco Africa-Atlantic Gas Pipeline, all contributing to strengthening economic and energy ties across the continent.

For human connectivity, the Moroccan Agency for International Cooperation (AMCI) facilitates South-South cooperation through training programs and scholarships. Morocco, granted ASEAN Sectoral Dialogue Partner status in 2023, aims to serve as a production and logistics hub near Europe and a gateway to African value chains, with concrete cooperation initiatives expected at the upcoming Morocco-ASEAN Sectoral Cooperation Committee meeting in Jakarta this fall.

ma.headline: Morocco observes 96% partial lunar eclipse before dawn Friday
ma.dek: A deep partial lunar eclipse will be visible across Morocco before dawn on Friday, August 28, with Earth’s shadow covering about 96% of the moon’s surface at its peak.
paragraphs: Morocco will experience a significant partial lunar eclipse early Friday morning, with the moon’s visible surface approximately 96.3% obscured by Earth’s shadow, according to NASA. The clearly visible partial phase is expected to begin around 3:34 a.m. local time, as the moon enters Earth’s dark central shadow, known as the umbra.

The maximum eclipse will occur at about 5:12 a.m., with the partial phase concluding near 6:52 a.m. The final stages of visibility will depend on local moonset times, with the moon setting in Casablanca around 7:10 a.m. Observers are advised to find a location with an unobstructed western horizon for the best view.

During the event, the darkened lunar surface may appear copper, orange, or deep red due to Earth’s atmosphere scattering blue light and bending red and orange light towards the moon. Unlike a total lunar eclipse, a narrow section of the moon will remain directly illuminated, preventing complete darkness, though its appearance may resemble a “blood moon.” Morocco’s next visible partial lunar eclipse is anticipated on January 12, 2028.

ug.headline: Uganda improves oversight of farm input suppliers
ug.dek: Fragmented regulatory oversight at the local government level has hindered the registration and licensing of agricultural input suppliers, impacting quality control and national.
paragraphs: Uganda is working to improve the oversight of agricultural input suppliers, particularly at the local government level, to address fragmentation in regulatory responsibilities. Currently, various directorates and departments, including crop, animal, fisheries, and agricultural planning, share the responsibility, making coordination difficult.

This scattered oversight has led to challenges in ensuring that input suppliers are registered and licensed, and that agricultural inputs undergo quality control testing to conform to national standards. The Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Industry and Fisheries (MAAIF) is the nationally mandated agency, but local execution has been inconsistent.

The lack of effective oversight means smallholder farmers often rely on informal networks, increasing their exposure to counterfeit inputs and price exploitation. Strengthening this oversight is critical for harmonizing coordination and improving compliance, ultimately aiming to boost agricultural productivity.

ug.headline: Uganda debates moving capital functions from Kampala to Nakasongola
ug.dek: A proposal to gradually relocate political and administrative functions from Kampala to a new urban center in Nakasongola is under consideration, reviving a long-standing debate.
paragraphs: The idea of moving some government functions from Kampala to Nakasongola has re-entered national discussion, according to contemporary reports in August 2026. This proposal suggests a phased relocation of ministries, departments, and agencies, potentially extending to 2040, with Kampala retaining its commercial role.

The debate over decentralizing government functions is not new, having surfaced periodically in Ugandan politics. In December 2024, Members of Parliament discussed this during the draft Fourth National Development Plan, with some suggesting moving Parliament to a new city like Nakasongola.

However, the proposal is not yet settled government policy, and a formal transfer of the capital would require a constitutional amendment under Article 5. Nakasongola is already identified in Uganda Vision 2040 as one of five strategic cities, but this designation does not equate to a decision to make it the national capital.

ug.headline: Katumba praises police cadet intake for producing top officers
ug.dek: Former Inspector General of Police Gen. (Rtd) Katumba Wamala commended the 2001 Uganda Police Force cadet intake for their 25 years of service and for developing dependable.
paragraphs: General Katumba Wamala, currently the Minister for Public Service, recognized 70 members of the 2001 police cadet intake during their silver jubilee celebration in Kampala. Katumba, who was Inspector General of Police when the cadets joined the force, stated that the group has produced reliable and useful officers for the Uganda Police Force.

The celebration marked 25 years since the cadets reported to the Police Training School in Kibuli on August 18, 2001. AIGP (Rtd) Grace Akullo, a member of the intake and former Director of the Criminal Investigations Directorate, highlighted the group's transformation from cadets to commanders, attributing their success to discipline, hard work, and resilience.

The intake has contributed officers to various leadership, command, and strategic positions within the Police Force, including the late AIGP Andrew Felix Kaweesi and AIGP (Rtd) Grace Akullo. Katumba encouraged the members, many of whom are nearing retirement, to cultivate a saving culture and prepare financially for life after active service.

ug.headline: Ugandan families dispute inheritance as wealth transfers spark legal concerns
ug.dek: Recent social media discussions and legal podcasts highlight growing concerns among wealthy Ugandans about property disputes and inheritance planning.
paragraphs: Disputes over inheritance are prompting wealthy Ugandans to re-evaluate estate planning, following viral social media videos where a son accused his mother of contributing to his prominent businessman father's death over wealth. This incident, coupled with another case where a son sued his still-living wealthy father to manage his business empire, has sparked widespread discussion on property distribution.

Lawyers are responding to the public interest by hosting podcasts and X Spaces to discuss wills and inheritance laws. One lawyer from a prominent Kampala firm advised individuals to allocate a portion of their wealth for their own enjoyment before death, suggesting a thirty percent allocation for themselves to prevent living miserably while preserving everything for their children.

These discussions reveal a common challenge for families, regardless of their wealth, as children often dispute wills, forge documents, or cause chaos when not named as heirs. Some children even forcibly occupy or sell estate properties, sometimes dislodging surviving parents or siblings, underscoring the complex family dynamics surrounding inherited wealth.

zw.headline: Reserve Bank reports Zimbabwe Gold inflation at 2.9% in August
zw.dek: Zimbabwe's annual Zimbabwe Gold (ZiG) inflation rate dropped to 2.9% in August, marking the lowest single-digit inflation recorded since 1980.
paragraphs: The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe (RBZ) announced that the annual ZiG inflation rate fell to 2.9% in August, a 0.3 percentage-point decline from July's 3.2%. This figure represents the lowest single-digit inflation outturn since 1980, according to the central bank.

Central bank governor John Mushayavanhu stated that the low ZiG inflation demonstrates the effectiveness of prudent policies in achieving price, currency, and exchange rate stability. The RBZ noted that the muted impact of a global oil price shock on Zimbabwe's inflation benefited from anchored inflation expectations, unlike other sub-Saharan African countries that saw increases of two to four percentage points.

The central bank highlighted that prices of domestic goods and services have increased at a similar pace in both ZiG and US dollars since August 2025. This implies businesses should be indifferent to pricing and accepting payments in either currency, supporting predictability for business planning and investment, which is critical for wider ZiG use in the multi-currency environment.

zw.headline: RBZ reports 91% surge in capital outflows to US$866 million
zw.dek: Zimbabwe's capital outflows nearly doubled in the first half of 2026, driven by increased external debt repayments and disinvestments, according to the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe.
paragraphs: Zimbabwe experienced a significant increase in capital outflows, with outward remittances surging 91% to US$866 million in the first half of 2026, up from US$453,6 million during the same period last year. This rise was primarily due to companies stepping up external debt repayments, as reported by the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe (RBZ) in its mid-term monetary policy review.

The RBZ also noted a 162,1% increase in disinvestments, reaching US165,5 million, and a 74,7% rise in foreign investment outflows to US79,6 million. External loan repayments grew by 80% to US$621 million. These figures indicate that companies are moving more capital offshore rather than reinvesting it domestically, at a time when the country aims to attract foreign direct investment.

Total foreign payments processed through banks increased by 44,9% to US7,3 billion in the first six months of 2026, compared to US5 billion in the corresponding period of 2025. Trade-related payments accounted for 81% of this total, reflecting a heavy reliance on imported goods and services, with 37% directed towards raw materials, intermediate goods, and capital goods.

zw.headline: IMF reports Zimbabwe's gold incentive spending exceeds budget by US$125 million
zw.dek: Zimbabwe's gold incentive scheme for artisanal miners spent US$141 million by April, nearly nine times its annual budget of US$16 million, according to the International Monetary.
paragraphs: Zimbabwe's gold incentive program for artisanal miners has significantly overshot its budget, reaching US$141 million by the end of April. This figure is US$125 million above the US$16 million allocated for the entire year, as reported by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in its first review under Zimbabwe’s Staff-Monitored Programme.

The incentives, introduced in 2021 to combat gold smuggling, consumed US$118 million in the first quarter alone. The IMF highlighted this fiscal overrun as a major challenge, alongside other spending pressures like front-loaded pension expenditures and capital spending that included a US$95 million net repayment of unaudited arrears.

This situation presents a policy dilemma for the government: cutting incentives might increase smuggling, while maintaining current spending levels risks further widening the gap between planned and actual expenditures. The IMF noted that protected social spending also fell US$84 million below the agreed program floor.

zw.dek: The African Export-Import Bank reported a significant increase in net income, reaching US534,7million, driven by expanded lending and stronger interest income.
paragraphs: Afreximbank announced a 30% rise in net income for the first six months of 2026, reaching US534,7million, up from US412,7 million in the same period last year. This growth was attributed to increased lending activities and higher interest income, despite ongoing inflationary pressures, according to the bank.

The bank's total assets and contingencies grew by 7,8% to US52,3billion from US48,5 billion at the end of 2025, primarily due to expanding lending. Net loans and advances increased by 5,7% to US35,4billion from US33,5 billion. Asset quality improved, with the non-performing loan ratio decreasing to 2,20% from 2,43% at year-end 2025.

Shareholders’ funds increased to US8,5billion from US8,4 billion, supported by internally generated profits and US13,9 million in new equity. Net interest income climbed 22% to US1,0billion from US840 million, while fee and commission income rose 15% to US71,1million from US61,9 million, reflecting higher earnings from guarantees, letters of credit, and advisory services.

cv.headline: Health Minister attends WHO meeting, seeks partnerships for national health system
cv.dek: Cape Verde's Minister of Health is in Ethiopia representing the country at the 76th Session of the WHO Regional Committee for Africa, aiming to strengthen international.
paragraphs: Cape Verde's Minister of Health is participating in the 76th Session of the WHO Regional Committee for Africa in Ethiopia, a move the government states is part of its strategy to enhance international cooperation and consolidate partnerships. The goal is to promote a more modern, efficient, and equitable national health system, according to a note sent to Inforpress.

During the session, Cape Verde is engaging in high-level debates on strengthening national health systems, emergency preparedness, universal health coverage, digital transformation, sustainable financing, and health security. The country's presence also allows for sharing national experiences and best practices, aiming to boost regional cooperation and project Cape Verde as an active partner in health promotion on the continent.

The Minister's agenda includes bilateral meetings with representatives from various countries and institutions to deepen cooperation and identify new partnership opportunities for health sector development in Cape Verde. The Minister will also attend the Inaugural Meeting of the Reconstituted Monitoring Committee of the African Public Health Emergency Fund and a Ministerial Dialogue, initiatives focused on reinforcing regional coordination and resource mobilization for health emergencies.

cv.headline: Cape Verde and China sign agreement to boost media cooperation
cv.dek: The new partnership will deepen collaboration in social communication, focusing on content sharing and professional exchange in radio, television, and online audiovisual platforms.
paragraphs: Cape Verde and China have signed an agreement to enhance cooperation in the social communication sector, as announced on Tuesday, August twenty-fifth, by the Ministry of Justice, Presidency of the Council of Ministers, Parliamentary Affairs and Social Communication. The accord was signed by Clóvis Silva, the Minister of Justice, Presidency of the Council of Ministers, Parliamentary Affairs and Social Communication, during his participation in the Seventh Forum on China-Africa Media Cooperation. This event took place in Beijing from August nineteenth to twenty-first, under the theme “Sharing development opportunities, shaping the audiovisual future.”

Beyond content sharing, the partnership includes the exchange of experiences and knowledge among professionals, as well as training and capacity-building initiatives in social communication. It also covers technological innovation and digital transformation, reflecting the rapid evolution of media and communication platforms, aiming to create new collaboration opportunities.

cv.headline: António Costa urges EU budget agreement by year-end
cv.dek: António Costa, president of the institution that unites European leaders, called for a political agreement on the EU's long-term budget for 2028-2034 by the end of 2026.
paragraphs: António Costa declared that this autumn will be decisive for the EU, as leaders work towards approving the European budget for the period 2028-2037. Speaking in Bratislava alongside Slovakia's Prime Minister Robert Fico, Costa emphasized that the budget is a political choice about the future of Europe. He urged European leaders to approach the final stages of this debate with open minds and a spirit of collective responsibility.

Costa, on a tour of European capitals to discuss the community budget, highlighted that the next Multiannual Financial Framework for 2028-2034 should prioritize competitiveness, industrial transformation, defense, security, and strategic resilience. He also stressed the need for effective use of funds for cohesion policy and the common agricultural policy, while ensuring reasonable contributions from member states.

The European Commission proposed an EU budget for 2028-2034 of two billion euros in July 2025. The Cypriot presidency of the Council of the EU, which ended in June, proposed a budget of one billion, nine hundred and forty billion euros. The European Parliament advocates for a budget of two billion, fourteen billion euros. Negotiations are ongoing, with a revised proposal expected from the current Irish presidency in October.

td.headline: Chadian court postpones General Miskine's trial to August 2026
td.dek: The trial of General Abdoulaye Miskine and his co-accused has been rescheduled by the N’Djamena high court due to heavy rainfall and a public holiday.
paragraphs: The trial of General Abdoulaye Miskine, also known as Martin Koumtamadji, and his co-accused has been postponed to August 26, 2026. The N’Djamena high court cited heavy rainfall on August 24, 2026, and the commemoration of Mawlid an-nabaoui on August 25, 2026, as reasons for the delay. Miskine has been detained for nearly seven years without judgment at Klessoum prison.

Miskine, along with Adoum Rakhis, Ringo Djouma, and Abdel-Aziz Gros, faces serious charges including assassinations, rapes, and insurrectional movements in the border area between Chad and the Central African Republic. The Chadian state is a civil party in this case, which is also closely watched in the Central African Republic.

A team of 10 lawyers will defend the accused, who benefit from the presumption of innocence. Miskine's defense has repeatedly raised concerns about his critical health, noting kidney failure and significant weight loss during his detention.

td.headline: CNDH urges calm after intercommunal violence in Oum-Hadjer
td.dek: Chad's National Commission for Human Rights (CNDH) called for restraint and legal resolution after deadly intercommunal clashes in Oum-Hadjer, Batha province.
paragraphs: The National Commission for Human Rights (CNDH) expressed deep concern regarding the situation in Oum-Hadjer, Batha province, following violent intercommunal clashes that resulted in deaths, injuries, and arrests. In a communiqué published on August twenty-fourth, two thousand twenty-six, the CNDH stated it is closely monitoring these events and urged all parties to show restraint and work towards peace.

The Commission encouraged affected communities to use legal and judicial channels to resolve disputes instead of resorting to violence. It also called on administrative, judicial, security, and traditional authorities to continue efforts to identify and prosecute those responsible for the crimes committed by all sides.

CNDH President Belngar Larmé Jacques signed the communiqué, which also extended condolences to the bereaved families and wished a speedy recovery to the injured. The institution emphasized the need to preserve peace, guarantee fundamental rights, and allow justice to establish accountability.

td.dek: The Chadian agro-food company introduced ZEINA Tomato 70g and ZEINA Macaroni 500g at a commercial meeting in N'Djamena, aiming to expand its national market presence.
paragraphs: MENA FOOD CHAD, a Chadian agro-food company, launched two new products under its ZEINA brand on Monday, August twenty-fourth, 2026. The new offerings, ZEINA Tomato 70g and ZEINA Macaroni 500g, were presented at a commercial meeting held in a capital hotel. The company emphasized its commitment to local production to serve food sovereignty and the local economy.

The ZEINA Tomato 70g is a compact and economical concentrated tomato format, designed to meet the purchasing power and daily needs of households, particularly for single-unit purchases common in retail and informal markets. ZEINA Macaroni 500g is a family-sized pasta, presented as a locally manufactured alternative to imported products, focusing on quality, cooking texture, and price.

MENA FOOD CHAD, based in N'Djamena, specializes in consumer goods like pasta and tomato concentrate. The company plans to strengthen its distribution network in N'Djamena and secondary cities including Moundou, Sarh, Abéché, Kélo, Doba, Oum-Hadjer, Massakory, and Mongo. It also intends to support wholesalers and retailers with commercial tools adapted to the Chadian market.

dj.headline: Djibouti urges collective action against youth vaping
dj.dek: Parents, teachers, and school officials are called upon to increase vigilance and awareness regarding the dangers of electronic cigarettes among minors.
paragraphs: Djibouti authorities are addressing the growing issue of youth vaping, emphasizing that electronic cigarettes are not harmless and should not be shared among peers. The Agence Djiboutienne d'Information reports that minors are obtaining these devices by finding them unattended, receiving them from friends, or purchasing them from vendors who disregard age restrictions.

The call for action highlights a collective responsibility, urging parents to keep electronic cigarettes out of children's reach and to monitor for behavioral changes. In schools, teachers and administrators are encouraged to reinforce awareness campaigns and educate students about the associated risks of vaping.

The message to young people is direct: do not use electronic cigarettes because they appear innocuous, are offered by a friend, or simply because of their taste. Preventing the normalization of vaping among minors requires a combination of information, vigilance, and open dialogue between parents, educators, and youth.

dj.headline: Djibouti hosts C STAR program, develops young African entrepreneurs
dj.dek: The fourth edition of the C STAR program, focused on youth entrepreneurship, launched in Djibouti, bringing together 32 young participants from 19 African countries.
paragraphs: Djibouti is hosting the fourth edition of the C STAR program, a pan-African platform for developing entrepreneurial skills and leadership among young people. The program, launched in 2022, has already trained over 1,500 participants from more than 50 African countries, with 45% being women. This year, 32 young people from 19 African nations were selected from 641 applicants across 44 countries.

The ceremony in Djibouti included several dignitaries, such as Aboubaker Omar Hadi, President of the Djibouti Ports and Free Zones Authority (DPFZA), and Miao Jianmin, President of China Merchants Group. Also present were Djiboutian ministers Said Nouh Hassan (Infrastructure and Equipment), Ilyas Moussa Dawaleh (Economy and Finance), and Safia Mohamed Ali Gadileh (Digital Economy and Innovation).

The C STAR program, implemented with the China Merchants Charity Foundation, UNDP, and the CLE Center, aims to foster a new generation of African leaders in innovation, entrepreneurship, and sustainable growth. It aligns with the Beijing Action Plan of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation (FOCAC) for 2025-2027, connecting young entrepreneurs with networks, investors, and economic opportunities across the continent.

sz.headline: Low Wages Force Textile Workers into Transactional Sex for E20
sz.dek: A new study reveals that some textile workers in Eswatini engage in transactional sex for as little as E20 due to insufficient wages to cover basic monthly expenses.
paragraphs: A study presented by the National Emergency Response Council on HIV and AIDS (NERCHA) at the Emafini Conference Centre found that low wages compel some textile workers to offer sex for E20. This finding emerged from the HIV Prevention Indaba study, which investigated factors influencing HIV prevention among various population groups across the country.

Textile workers interviewed for the study reported that their remuneration is too low to meet their needs, leading some to engage in transactional sex for money to buy necessities like bread or pay for electricity. One worker suggested government intervention to ensure textile firms pay employees better, highlighting the choice between dignity and survival when faced with immediate financial offers.

The study emphasizes that these economic pressures increase vulnerability to HIV, particularly among young women in the textile sector. It points to the need for interventions that address the economic circumstances driving these behaviors, rather than focusing solely on health messaging, to improve HIV prevention efforts in the country.

sz.headline: Eswatini Government Plans E1.5 Billion Debt Amid Inequality Concerns
sz.dek: The Eswatini government intends to raise an additional E1.5 billion this financial year to fund capital projects, even as economic growth disproportionately benefits the wealthy.
paragraphs: Finance Minister Neal Rijkenberg announced the government's plan to secure E1.5 billion to address financial pressures and support capital projects. This comes as the country's total public debt decreased by E652.48 million between March and June, settling at E41.84 billion, or 40.47 per cent of GDP, by the end of June.

Despite an expected economic growth of 5.6 per cent in 2025, Minister for Economic Planning and Development Dr Thambo Gina acknowledged that this growth is not translating into improved living standards for ordinary citizens. He attributed this to high income and wealth inequality, where benefits are concentrated among a small segment of society.

Gina highlighted that major public and private investments, including renewable energy, the Mkhondvo-Ngwavuma Water Augmentation Project, new Central Bank facilities, and textile and agribusiness investments, are driving the growth. However, he stressed the need for more inclusive economic growth to ensure benefits reach a broader range of households, as many emaSwati remain below the poverty line.

sz.headline: Namibia pledges support for Eswatini's research council
sz.dek: Namibia will provide continued assistance to Eswatini as the kingdom works to establish its National Research Council and strengthen its national research, science, technology.
paragraphs: Namibia has committed to supporting Eswatini's efforts to operationalize its National Research Council (NRC) and enhance its research, science, technology, and innovation system. Dr. Nhlanhla Lupahla, General Manager for Research, Science, Technology and Innovation Coordination and Support at Namibia’s National Commission on Research, Science and Technology, stated that Namibia is prepared to share its experiences and lessons with Eswatini during a capacity strengthening workshop.

Lupahla emphasized that Namibia views the establishment of Eswatini's council as a significant investment in the kingdom's capacity to utilize research, science, technology, and innovation to address national development priorities. He noted that the two countries share historical and regional ties, along with similar institutional environments, opportunities, and challenges in developing national research and innovation systems.

Namibia's support will also extend to the continental science and research community, with Namibia hosting the Science Granting Councils Initiative (SGCI) All Partners Meeting in Windhoek from September 27 to October 3, 2026. During this meeting, Namibia plans to support Eswatini's admission into the SGCI network, which is expected to strengthen Eswatini's research ecosystem and contribute to the collective voice of science granting councils across Africa.

sz.headline: PLE schedules 8Bet Trade Fair Cup during CAF matches
sz.dek: The Premier League of Eswatini (PLE) has created a fixture conflict by scheduling its 8Bet Trade Fair Cup during the CAF Champions League and CAF Confederation Cup preliminary.
paragraphs: The Premier League of Eswatini (PLE) has scheduled the 8Bet Trade Fair Cup to coincide with the first preliminary rounds of the CAF Champions League and CAF Confederation Cup, according to the Times of Eswatini. This decision appears to contradict CAF Inter-club Competitions Regulations, which state that CAF matches take priority over other fixtures.

PLE chairman Polycarp Dlamini acknowledged the clash involving Eswatini’s CAF envoys, Nsingizini Hotspurs and Green Mamba, but stated that clubs must plan to participate in both competitions. Green Mamba, representing Eswatini in the CAF Confederation Cup, is scheduled to play a domestic quarter-final on September 3 and a semi-final on September 5, the same day as their CAF Confederation Cup first-leg match against 1º de Agosto.

Green Mamba Chief Executive Officer Ntuthuko Dlamini confirmed the club is aware of CAF regulations but intends to participate in both, awaiting guidance from the PLE if a clash materializes. The 8Bet Trade Fair Cup is aligned with the Eswatini International Trade Fair calendar and has a new three-year agreement through 2031.

sz.headline: Gin Gardens 2026 Expands Entertainment and Lifestyle Offerings in Ezulwini
sz.dek: The Gin Gardens event on October 3, 2026, will feature a diverse lineup of international and local artists, food, and art experiences for over 1,500 guests at Sharma House.

A partnership with Phillz Art will introduce live painting and art giveaways for VIP guests, creating an interactive and creative dimension to the overall experience.

ga.headline: Teenager receives prison sentence for mother's involuntary homicide in Franceville
ga.dek: A 13-year-old girl, G.M., was sentenced to 12 months in prison, with seven months suspended, and a three million CFA franc fine for the involuntary homicide of her mother, Esther.
paragraphs: The Franceville Court of First Instance, sitting as a criminal court for children, convicted G.M. on August 19 for the death of her mother, which occurred on June 13, 2024, in Okondja. G.M. admitted to putting camphor in her mother's drink to make her sleep, intending to go out at night without parental supervision. Her mother, Esther Diki Nzoghet, fell ill after consuming the drink and later died at the city's medical center.

Investigations by the local gendarmerie brigade quickly focused on G.M., who remained consistent in her statements throughout the preliminary inquiry, instruction, and hearing. She confessed to the act, stating she no longer tolerated her mother's reprimands regarding her nighttime outings and romantic relationship. The court considered her young age and the absence of intent to kill, leading to a conviction for involuntary homicide rather than poisoning.

G.M. was placed in pre-trial detention at Franceville central prison on June 21, 2024, where she spent approximately six months before being granted provisional release. Her lawyer, Maitre Yoni Andy Nkum’Enguie, acknowledged her guilt and advocated for a suspended sentence, while the public prosecutor requested leniency due to her age.

ga.headline: Immongault advances forest and 'Gabon Infini' initiatives
ga.dek: Vice President Hermann Immongault led two working sessions to finalize funding for ecosystem preservation and address challenges in the timber sector.
paragraphs: Gabon's Vice President, Hermann Immongault, chaired two working sessions on Monday, August twenty-fourth, focusing on recommendations for the "Gabon Infini" financing project and issues within the timber industry. The government aims to finalize an agreement with funders and boost the competitiveness of Gabonese forest products in international markets.

The first session addressed recommendations from the sixth steering committee meeting for the "Gabon Infini" performance financing project. This project supports Gabon's commitment to preserve and enhance 30% of its coastal, terrestrial, and marine ecosystems, backed by a 200 million dollar fund, partly financed by the Gabonese state.

The second session focused on presidential directives for the timber sector, following a recent meeting between the President and industry operators. Immongault stated the goal is to restore sector competitiveness, enhance national resource value, save jobs, increase economic contribution, and establish the "Bois du Gabon" brand for quality.

ga.headline: US Judge Invalidates Visa Suspension for 75 Nations, Including Gabon
ga.dek: A New York federal judge on Friday, August 21, 2026, invalidated the Trump administration's decision to suspend immigration visa processing for citizens of 75 countries.
paragraphs: The ruling by Judge Jeannette Vargas halts a key part of the White House's migration policy, finding that the executive branch overstepped its authority by targeting applicants based on financial criteria. This decision affects individuals seeking to settle permanently in the United States, including those from countries like Nigeria, Afghanistan, Somalia, Brazil, and Iran.

The US administration had cited financial risk as the basis for the policy, considering some immigration candidates likely to depend on social benefits or burden public finances. Consular services, including the US Embassy in Libreville, were instructed to suspend procedures, even for applicants who met other requirements, forcing Gabonese applicants to travel to third countries like Equatorial Guinea or DR Congo.

The New York judge's decision means that visa refusals based solely on this policy can no longer be maintained. This judgment represents another setback for Donald Trump's efforts to reduce immigration to the United States, as his administration's policies frequently face challenges and suspensions in the courts.

ga.headline: Four unions form new federation for extractive and energy workers
ga.dek: The Force ouvrière des industries extractives et énergétiques (FOIEE) was established in Libreville to represent workers in Gabon's oil, gas, water, electricity, and mining.
paragraphs: Four major trade unions in Gabon's extractive and energy sectors ratified the statutes of a new federation, the Force ouvrière des industries extractives et énergétiques (FOIEE), on August twenty-third, two thousand twenty-six, in Libreville. This new organization aims to consolidate the representation of workers in these strategic industries.

The founding members include ONEP for oil and gas, SYNTEE+ of SEEG for water and electricity, and SYLTRAC and SYNATIEX for mining workers at COMILOG. Sylvain Mayabi Binet was named Secretary General, leading an eight-member federal executive bureau. The federation intends to leverage the strong representation of its founding unions from recent professional elections.

According to Secretary General Sylvain Mayabi Binet, the election results confirm the influence of these organizations within the extractive, energy, and mining industries. This positions the FOIEE as a significant participant in social dialogue across these sectors, affecting thousands of workers in Gabon.

ga.headline: Former Prosecutor Eddy Narcisse Minang removed from magistracy
ga.dek: Eddy Narcisse Minang, who led the Bongo trial in November 2025, has been struck from the judicial register due to alleged embezzlement and judicial interference.
paragraphs: Eddy Narcisse Minang, the former Attorney General and lead prosecutor in the high-profile Bongo trial, was removed from the magistracy this week. This decision follows accusations of embezzlement in a case involving a Chinese businessman and alleged judicial interferences, including in the Ministry of National Education's treasury bond affair, according to a source close to the Ministry of Justice.

Minang was among ten magistrates summoned by a disciplinary council on Tuesday but did not appear, leading to the decision being made without his testimony. He had been previously suspended from his duties by the Minister of Justice on June 9, 2026, over similar allegations. His relatives claim these accusations are a political maneuver linked to the Bongo trial.

During the Bongo trial, which was broadcast live on national television, Minang sought twenty years of criminal imprisonment for massive embezzlement of public funds against Sylvia and Noureddin Bongo. This sentence was subsequently pronounced in absentia against the mother and son duo.

gm.headline: Darboe links UDP history to call for unity and electoral reform
gm.dek: United Democratic Party leader Ousainou Darboe used the party's 30th anniversary rally to advocate for political change and national unity ahead of the December 5 presidential.
paragraphs: Ousainou Darboe, leader of the United Democratic Party (UDP), addressed thousands of supporters at the party’s 30th anniversary rally in Brikama, emphasizing the UDP’s history of sacrifices. He recalled instances of imprisonment, violence, and deaths endured by party members, particularly during former President Yahya Jammeh’s 22-year rule, to highlight the cost of challenging authoritarianism.

Darboe specifically mentioned the 1996 ambush at Denton Bridge, where several young members were tortured, and the arrest of Amadou Sanneh for refusing to support the APRC government. He also paid tribute to Solo Sandeng, a UDP activist who died in state custody in April 2016 after campaigning for electoral reforms, noting that some of these reforms, like the Public Order Act, remain unfinished nearly a decade later.

Looking forward to the upcoming presidential election, Darboe called for opposition unity and urged Gambians to reject ethnic divisions. He pledged that a UDP government would increase representation for persons with disabilities in senior government positions, enhance support for farmers, and prioritize agriculture, framing the anniversary as a reminder of ongoing political struggles.

gm.headline: Three survive Jimpex Road crash, one passenger seriously injured
gm.dek: A road accident at Jimpex today left one passenger seriously injured after becoming trapped inside a vehicle that collided with a parked car.
paragraphs: Three individuals, including a driver and two passengers, survived a road accident earlier today at Jimpex. One front-seat passenger sustained serious injuries after being pinned inside the wreckage, with his legs stuck following the impact.

Eyewitnesses reported that the car, traveling from Banjul, struck another vehicle parked along the roadside. While the driver and a rear-seat passenger escaped unharmed, rescue efforts were challenging for the trapped passenger.

Emergency responders eventually freed the injured passenger, who was then rushed to the hospital for treatment. An eyewitness credited the airbag and seatbelt for preventing more severe injuries, stating, “The airbag and the seat belt saved him. If not, his head would have hit the car.” No fatalities were recorded, though the exact circumstances remain unclear, highlighting ongoing road safety concerns in The Gambia.

gm.headline: Central Bank cuts policy rate to 14 percent amid economic growth
gm.dek: The Central Bank of The Gambia reduced its Monetary Policy Rate to 14 percent in February 2026, maintaining it through August, as the economy expanded by 5.9 percent in 2025.
paragraphs: The Central Bank of The Gambia has lowered its Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) from 17 percent to 14 percent by February 2026, holding it steady through August. This decision follows a reduction from 17 percent to 16 percent in December 2025, aiming to balance inflation, economic activity, and financial stability.

The rate cuts occur as The Gambia's economy shows broad-based growth. The World Bank estimates a 5.9 percent growth in 2025, building on 5.6 percent in 2024, with contributions from agriculture, industry, and services. Tourism has recovered, remittances remain significant, and inflation has returned to single-digit figures.

Despite positive economic indicators, including a projected 5.3 percent growth by the World Bank for 2026, concerns persist regarding the nation's domestic debt. gm.headline: Gambian Muslims commemorate Prophet Muhammad's birth with gamo gatherings
gm.dek: Muslims across The Gambia will gather today, August 25th, for gamo celebrations, with August 26th declared a public holiday to honor the birth of the Holy Prophet Muhammad.
paragraphs: Today, August 25th, Muslims in The Gambia are observing gamo to commemorate the birth of the Holy Prophet Muhammad. Homes, mosques, and communities are hosting recitations of the Holy Qur’an, salawaat, sermons, and khassaïdes. This celebration extends across the border to Tivaouane, Medina Baye, and Touba, which will also become centers of prayer and remembrance.

The commemoration emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's teachings on faith, honesty, prayer, compassion, justice, and forgiveness. He is described in the Holy Qur’an as “a mercy to the worlds” and “an excellent example” for believers, known for his great moral character and care for the vulnerable.

The event also serves as a call for self-examination, particularly relevant as The Gambia approaches a presidential election. Concerns about divisive political and ethnic rhetoric highlight the importance of preserving national cohesion, encouraging citizens to maintain brotherhood despite differences, consistent with the Prophet's message against tribal superiority and injustice.

gn.headline: Guinean Government announces emergency measures after Dar-es-Salam landslide
gn.dek: Following a deadly landslide at the Dar-es-Salam landfill, the Guinean government has implemented emergency measures to secure the site, assist victims, and rehouse affected.
paragraphs: The Guinean government announced a series of emergency measures this Tuesday, August twenty-fifth, 2026, to address the aftermath of a landslide at the Dar-es-Salam landfill. These actions include securing the site, providing care for victims, and organizing the rehousing of populations at risk, as stated by the Minister of Territorial Administration and Decentralization, Madame Camara Djénabou Touré.

The measures involve deploying mixed teams to identify and survey at-risk homes near the landfill and immediately securing the perimeter to prevent further incidents. The Ministry of Health has set up medical provisions and is distributing mosquito nets to those affected. Additionally, a collective burial for the victims of the tragedy will be organized.

Currently, 542 displaced individuals are housed at Dixinn Centre 1 primary school, and approximately 1,500 people requiring rehousing have been identified. The government plans to demolish the Dar-es-Salam landfill completely in the coming days and identify new relocation sites across Conakry for the affected residents.

gn.headline: Six bound bodies found in Forécariah mass grave
gn.dek: Six unidentified men were discovered blindfolded and with their hands tied in a mass grave in a forest area of Sabakhouré, Allassoyah sub-prefecture, on Monday, August.
paragraphs: The discovery of six bound and blindfolded male bodies in a mass grave in Sabakhouré has prompted an investigation by local authorities. The bodies, found in a forest area, were transported to the Forécariah prefectural hospital for examination to determine their identities and the circumstances of their deaths.

Ibrahima Soriba Touré, the local mayor, confirmed the discovery after being alerted by a sector chief about unusual signs at a work site. The sub-prefect, police commissioner, and prosecutor were informed and visited the scene, where they found the six unidentified individuals.

The incident has caused shock and concern among residents in the Forécariah prefecture. An inquiry is expected to shed light on the exact circumstances surrounding the deaths, as the identities of the victims and the cause of death remain unknown.

gn.headline: President Doumbouya decorates former CNT members for national service
gn.dek: President Mamadi Doumbouya awarded honorary distinctions to former members of the National Council of the Transition (CNT) for their service from January 22, 2022, to July 17.
paragraphs: Conakry, Guinea – President Mamadi Doumbouya has honored former members of the National Council of the Transition (CNT) with medals, according to decrees read on state media this Tuesday, August twenty-fifth. The decorations recognize “eminent services rendered to the Nation” by the recipients during their tenure.

The awards elevate several key figures from the transitional parliamentary institution to various national orders. Dr. Dansa Kourouma, former President of the CNT, was named Grand Officer of the National Order of the Kolatier. Professor Elhadj Hassan Bah, president of the Health, Education, Social Affairs, and Cultural Commission, received the rank of Commander of the National Order of the Kolatier.

Additionally, Madame Hadja Maimouna Yombouno, the first Vice-President of the CNT, was decorated as a Commander of the National Order of Merit. Other former cabinet members, bureau members, and advisors of the CNT were also elevated to the rank of Commander of the National Order of Merit for their contributions to the nation.
